## 1. [A statistical study of ionized outflows in low-mass galaxies from DESI DR1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15884) <a id="link1"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15884

**Authors:** Michael Romano, Amélie Saintonge, Chiara Circosta, Claudia Cicone, Darko Donevski, Dirk Scholte, Bendix Hagedorn

**Abstract:** We present a statistical analysis of ionized gas outflows in a large sample of low-mass ($\mathrm{log(M_{*}/M_{\odot})\lesssim10}$) galaxies at $z<0.45$ from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). Using [OIII] and H$\alpha$ emission lines, we identify $\sim5800$ dwarf galaxies with robust signatures of ionized outflows. Most are star-forming systems above the star-forming main sequence, with a smaller fraction of composites and AGN hosts. The derived mass-loading factors span $\eta=0.001-1$, with a median $\eta\sim0.01$, consistent with previous studies at similar stellar masses. These values are $1$--$2$ dex lower than predicted by cosmological simulations, suggesting that the ionized phase traces only a minor fraction of the total outflow mass. Outflow velocities are sufficient to enrich the circumgalactic medium in $\gtrsim80\%$ of cases, while escape into the intergalactic medium appears efficient mainly in composite and AGN hosts. We find that mass-loading factors decrease with stellar mass, broadly reproducing simulated trends despite the normalization offset. Comparing individual detections with stacked spectra of the general low-mass star-forming population, we find systematically lower mass-loading factors in the stacks, although the difference decreases toward larger offsets above the star-forming main sequence. Together with a positive correlation between mass-loading factor and specific star-formation rate, this suggests that enhanced star formation and burstiness regulate feedback efficiency and shape galactic winds. Our results highlight the role of ionized outflows in the baryon cycle of low-mass galaxies and the need for multiphase studies to fully understand feedback in galaxy evolution.

**Comment:** Star-formation-driven ionized outflows in dwarf galaxies, mass-loading factors

**Relevance:** 10
**Novelty:** 8

**Abstract:** We searched within the first data release of the Euclid Wide Survey (~1900 deg^2) for resolved stellar systems between distances from 10 kpc and several Mpc, using an isochrone filtering technique. We detect 15 systems that have never been resolved into stars before. Five are new discoveries, three in the Milky Way halo and two beyond the Local Group. The remaining ten are dwarf galaxies that were previously catalogued as unresolved sources in shallower ground-based surveys and lack reliable distance measures. We measured distance moduli for all 15 systems, and half-light radii, ellipticities, position angles, absolute magnitudes, and stellar masses for 14 of them. In the Milky Way halo, Ursa Minor II, at ~20 kpc, has Mv ~ +2.0 and a stellar mass of ~40 Msun, and is one of the least luminous stellar systems known. Fornax 7 is located near the tidal limit of the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy and may be physically associated with it. Eridanus V lies at ~165 kpc and has a stellar mass of ~550 Msun, which places it in the region of the size-luminosity plane where globular clusters and ultra-faint dwarf galaxies overlap. Beyond the Local Group, the 12 dwarf galaxies lie at distances of 3--5.5 Mpc. Three of them reach or exceed a mean surface brightness within the half-light radius of mu_V~28 mag/arcsec^2, a regime in which almost no galaxies at these distances were previously known. Ten of them are candidate members of the M81 group: eight have three-dimensional distances from M81 smaller than or comparable to the radius of its zero-velocity surface, and two lie close to the peripheral member NGC 4236, one of which is a candidate satellite of this galaxy. These results demonstrate Euclid's transformative potential for low-surface-brightness science, enabling the study of an unprecedented range of environments from the MW halo out to the Local Volume within a single, homogeneous survey.

**Comment:** New dwarf galaxies, satellite luminosity function, near-field cosmology

**Relevance:** 9
**Novelty:** 8

## 3. [A giant dark matter core extending far beyond the stars of a dwarf galaxy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15528) <a id="link3"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15528

**Authors:** Qinwei Yuan, Yong Shi, Xin Li, Zhiyu Zhang, Zhiyuan Zheng, Qiusheng Gu, Xiaoling Yu, Fuyan Bian

**Abstract:** In the standard cosmological model, the distribution of cold dark matter (CDM) can be reshaped by baryonic processes through gravity, as gas outflows alter the central potential and transform steep cusps into nearly constant-density cores. However, such feedback-generated cores are generally expected to have sizes comparable to the visible stellar body of a galaxy. Here we report the discovery of an exceptionally extended dark matter core in a nearby gas-rich dwarf galaxy UGCA 320. We combine high-resolution MUSE H$\alpha$ kinematics in the inner region with high-, medium-, and low-resolution MeerKAT HI observations from the MHONGOOSE survey tracing the galaxy out to large radii. After accounting for an additional non-circular kinematic component identified in the central HI spectra, we construct an extended rotation curve to constrain the dark matter distribution. The resulting rotation curve is poorly reproduced by a cuspy Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) halo but well described by cored pseudo-isothermal (ISO) and Burkert halo models. Consistently, a fit with a generalized NFW model yields an inner density slope of $\gamma=0.36\pm0.12$, quantitatively supporting a shallow central density profile. The best-fit ISO model gives a dark matter core radius of $7.62\pm0.80$ kpc, approximately four times the stellar half-light radius and substantially larger than typically found in dwarf galaxies. We investigate the main systematic uncertainties and find that the resulting core radii remain large, all lying within 3$\sigma$ of the fiducial fit. The exceptionally large core in UGCA 320 may pose a challenge to the standard CDM paradigm. While its properties are broadly consistent with self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), they may be difficult to reconcile with warm and fuzzy dark matter models, as well as the stellar feedback-driven core formation scenario.

**Comment:** Dark matter core-cusp in dwarf galaxy

**Relevance:** 9
**Novelty:** 8

## 4. [Satellite pairs in the Local Group: from spatial clustering to dynamical associations in observations and $\Lambda$CDM simulations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16687) <a id="link4"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16687

**Authors:** Mariana P. Júlio, Marcel S. Pawlowski, Noam I. Libeskind

**Abstract:** We investigate the incidence and physical nature of satellite galaxy pairs in the Local Group using updated observational data for the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31), together with analogues from the HESTIA constrained cosmological simulations. Our comparison uses three distinct simulated Local Group analogues drawn from the HESTIA suite, allowing us to assess the observed pair statistics against multiple cosmological realisations of the Local Group environment. We identify close nearest-neighbour associations by comparing the observed satellite distributions with isotropic populations that reproduce the radial distributions of each host, and investigate their physical nature using line-of-sight velocities, proper motions, and gravitational binding estimates. We find that the MW exhibits a significant excess of close satellite associations relative to isotropic expectations, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim53\%$, nearly twice that found in the simulated analogues ($\sim17$-$27\%$). This excess persists after applying a stellar mass cut ($M_\star > 10^4\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) to match the resolution limits of the simulations. In contrast, the M31 satellite system is broadly consistent with isotropy, with a pairing efficiency of $\sim28\%$. However, only a minority of pair candidates exhibit coherent kinematics or are likely to be gravitationally bound, indicating that most represent transient alignments or remnants of common group infall rather than long-lived binary satellites. These results suggest that the MW hosts an unusually rich population of phase-space-correlated satellites, likely reflecting its recent accretion history, whereas M31 is more consistent with typical $\Lambda$CDM expectations.

**Comment:** Satellite pairs in Local Group, MW accretion history, near-field cosmology

**Relevance:** 9
**Novelty:** 7

## 5. [The Distant Milky Way Halo from the Southern Hemisphere: Spatially broad and closer stellar debris associated to the Magellanic Stream](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15301) <a id="link5"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15301

**Authors:** Manuel Cavieres, Jesús Torres, Camila Navarrete, Himansh Rathore, Julio Chanamé, Gurtina Besla, Nicolás Garavito-Camargo, A. Katherina Vivas

**Abstract:** The Magellanic Stream (MS) is a gaseous structure extending over $150^\circ$ across the sky, likely formed through interactions between the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) as they fell into the Milky Way (MW). Its predicted stellar counterpart would provide a collisionless record of these interactions, but few candidate members have been identified. To expand this sample, we constructed a catalog of 87,763 distant K-giant candidates using DELVE DR2 and VHS DR5 photometry and Gaia DR3 astrometry, and analyzed VLT and Magellan spectra of 51 targets along the trailing MS. Combining radial velocities, spectrophotometric distances, and proper motions, we identify five new MS candidates at 58--95 kpc. Their metallicities are consistent with the outskirts of the SMC, while orbit integrations in a time-dependent MW--LMC--SMC potential support a possible Magellanic origin. Combined with previously identified candidates, these stars span a substantially broader range of Magellanic latitude than predicted by existing models, suggesting an extended debris field rather than a narrow stream. The candidates also lie predominantly closer than the simulated debris. More recent, less eccentric SMC orbits may help explain this distance discrepancy, although new simulations are required to test their implications for the stellar debris, along with larger spectroscopic samples.

**Comment:** Magellanic Stream stellar debris, MW-LMC-SMC interaction, accreted halo

**Relevance:** 9
**Novelty:** 7

## 6. [Dark matter alters dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14638) <a id="link6"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14638

**Authors:** Akaxia Cruz, Robel Geda, Alyson Brooks, Mariangela Lisanti, Annika H. G. Peter, Thomas R. Quinn, Ben Keller

**Abstract:** Dwarf galaxies are the most dark-matter-dominated systems in the Universe, serving as unique laboratories for exploring the fundamental nature of the dark sector. Although the observed diversity in dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies suggests an interplay between dark matter and baryonic physics, this relationship has remained largely unquantified in existing models. Here, we utilize a set of novel cosmological simulations with baryons to demonstrate how dark matter physics directly drives the structural evolution of these galaxies. By comparing the same systems across cold dark matter and varied self-interacting dark matter models, we find that the evolution of the central density of dark matter significantly impacts a galaxy's half-light radius, but the signal is dependent on morphology. This causal link establishes galaxy size as a direct signature of the underlying dark matter microphysics. Our findings provide a predictive framework for decoding dark matter particle properties from galactic shapes, offering a roadmap for upcoming wide-field surveys, such as the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, to probe the dark sector through the statistical analysis of galaxy populations.

**Comment:** Dwarf galaxy simulations, dark matter core-cusp, sizes

**Relevance:** 8
**Novelty:** 7

## 7. [Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17204) <a id="link7"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17204

**Authors:** Praniti Singh, JiJi Fan, Savvas M. Koushiappas, Isabelle S. Goldstein

**Abstract:** Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

**Comment:** Dwarf galaxy stellar kinematics probing dark matter core-cusp

**Relevance:** 8
**Novelty:** 6

## 8. [La Silla-QUEST RR Lyrae Survey III: The Shape of the Outer Virgo Overdensity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14734) <a id="link8"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14734

**Authors:** R. Zinn (Department of Astronomy, Yale University), P. S. Coppi (Department of Astronomy, Yale University, Department of Physics, Yale University), C. Baltay (Department of Physics, Yale University), D. Rabinowitz (Department of Physics, Yale University), E. P. Bellinger (Department of Astronomy, Yale University), K. Bettwy (Department of Astronomy, Yale University)

**Abstract:** Using the La Silla-QUEST and Gaia surveys, we identify 256 RR Lyrae stars (RRLS) in the Outer Virgo Overdensity (OVOD). These show that the OVOD has a signifcantly larger and more complex shape than previously recognized. The OVOD lies at an average distance of $\sim 85$ kpc, has a long dimension of $\sim 57^\circ$ ($\sim 85$ kpc), and a width that varies from $\sim 10^\circ $ ($\sim 15$ kpc) to $\sim 35^\circ $ ($\sim 50$ kpc) in a prominent bulge. Because it bends by $\sim 35^\circ$ from a great circle, it does not appear to be a stellar stream. The type ab RRLS (RRab) span a large range in period, with a mean of $0.59$ days, and only $19\pm 3 \%$ lie near the locus of Oosterhoff II variables in the Bailey diagram. The overall large number of RRLS along with a mean RRab metallicity ([Fe/H]) of -1.60 and $1 \sigma$ dispersion of 0.32, as inferred from the RRab periods, suggest that the OVOD progenitor was a large dwarf galaxy. The hypothesis that the OVOD may be a shell produced by the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger \citep{chandra2023} is supported by the $\sim 70^\circ$ angle that the southern extension of the OVOD makes with the orbits of red giants in its central part. The complex shape of the overall RRLS distribution, including a small north-south distance gradient, may also indicate, however, that we are seeing a blended, composite structure projected on the sky.

**Comment:** RR Lyrae in outer Virgo Overdensity, accreted halo substructure

**Relevance:** 8
**Novelty:** 6

## 9. [Solar models using OPLIB monochromatic opacities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16669) <a id="link9"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16669

**Authors:** M. Vidal, M. Deal, O. Richard, Y. Lebreton, J. Wang, J. Colgan, C. J. Fontes

**Abstract:** Context. Opacity is a key ingredient in describing the transport of energy in stars. There are several methods for calculating stellar opacities, resulting in different tables (OPAL, OP, OPAS, and OPLIB). These opacities are available in two distinct forms: tables that regroup the Rosseland mean opacity pre-calculated at predefined chemical mixtures, and monochromatic opacity spectra of individual chemical elements, which allow for the computation of Rosseland mean opacity for a precise mixture. Aims. ## 16. [Discrete Supernovae and the Limits of Continuous Models in Low-Mass Dark Matter Halos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15335) <a id="link16"></a>

**Abstract:** Many galaxy formation models represent supernova feedback by a continuous energy injection rate averaged over the stellar initial mass function (IMF). This approximation can fail in low-mass dark matter halos, where single, discrete supernovae can unbind more gas than the reservoir holds. We investigate this using a one-zone model that characterises continuous and discrete supernova feedback at redshifts $z\geq5$. Both feedback modes inject the same expected energy per unit stellar mass formed. In the discrete model, individual supernovae are resolved and energy is injected instantaneously; in the continuous model, supernovae are IMF-averaged and energy injection is spread over a finite time interval. Once stars form, a supernova can unbind 1.5-2.7 times the gas present. Continuous feedback begins removing gas after $\sim 4$ Myr, whereas the first discrete supernova occurs after $\sim 10$ Myr, which produces a stellar mass excess before feedback takes effect. The excess persists because the reservoir responds nonlinearly: an event removes at most the gas present, and star formation halts once it is empty. It depends strongly on halo mass: from 135 per cent at $10^7\, \rm{M}_\odot$, to 15 per cent at $10^8\, \rm{M}_\odot$, to negligible at $10^9\, \rm{M}_\odot$ by $z=5$. Fixing the number and timing of supernovae does not remove the stellar excess, which indicates that it is not caused by stochastic IMF sampling. Instead, it vanishes when the same energy is divided among more, smaller events. Matching the energy released per unit stellar mass therefore does not guarantee equivalent feedback in halos that retain gas until the first supernova.

The age-metallicity relations consistently reveal two distinct components: an older population consistent with a self-enrichment scenario, and a younger population formed from gas inflows with a different chemical enrichment history. The empirical libraries produce a monotonic decline of metallicities from old to young populations, which would require a sustained inflow of metal-poor gas outpacing its own enrichment. The theoretical libraries instead recover a young component whose metallicity departs from the older populations only at the most recent ages and by a few tenths of a dex, compatible with a single dilution episode. Our results demonstrate that model choice critically affects inferred metallicities, with empirical stellar libraries recovering age-metallicity relations that demand physical conditions the gas measurements cannot sustain.

## 25. [Mitigating variance shrinkage in multi-task galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16598) <a id="link25"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16598

**Authors:** Zhijian Luo, Jianzhen Chen

**Abstract:** Inferring photometric redshifts ($z$) and key stellar population properties ($\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $D_n4000$, and $\mathrm{H}\delta_A$) directly from multi-band imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional point-wise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts non-linear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tail populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multi-scale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Trained on 83,846 galaxies from Subaru HSC five-band ($g,r,i,z,y$) imaging cross-matched with DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey spectra, the model achieves high point-estimate precision on an independent test set of 5,000 galaxies: $\sigma_{\mathrm{NMAD}} = 0.020$ for $z$, $0.169\,\mathrm{dex}$ for $\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $0.073$ for $D_n4000$, and $1.185\,\text{\r{A}}$ for $\mathrm{H}\delta_A$. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the MMD loss effectively mitigates variance shrinkage and more accurately reproduces the observed spectroscopic parameter distributions (including bimodal structures and heavy tails), while maintaining point-estimate accuracy statistically consistent with the baseline (RMSE changes $\le 3.5\%$) and catastrophic outlier rates fully comparable to the baseline. This kernel-based manifold alignment offers a statistically grounded and practical paradigm for comprehensive galaxy property inference in the deep imaging era.

## 26. [Dark Matter Velocimetry with Quantum Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15878) <a id="link26"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15878

**Authors:** Miguel Angel Soto Alcaraz, Doojin Kim, Kyoungchul Kong, Myeonghun Park

**Abstract:** Quantum sensor networks can use the spatial phase coherence of wavelike dark matter to probe not only particle properties but also the motion and structure of the Galactic halo. We explore this idea for the minimal two-node network, in which a nonlocal exchange measurement samples the characteristic function of the velocity distribution. We compare the Standard Halo Model (SHM) with a Gaia-inspired radially anisotropic component and their mixture (SHM++), taking into account daily and annual modulation, postselection, depolarizing events, and a flat instrumental offset. We show that annual modulation at one fixed local sidereal time has the same phase waveform for the centered SHM and Gaia-inspired SHM++ models, leaving them degenerate when the overall signal amplitude is unknown. Earth's rotation breaks this degeneracy by scanning the baseline through Galactic directions and exposing the direction-dependent coherence of an anisotropic population. Distinguishing these velocity distributions would test whether the local halo is smooth and nearly isotropic or contains a radially biased accreted component, turning a quantum-network detection into a probe of Milky Way structure. Our likelihood analysis shows how modulation and signal-odd controls separate this information from flat backgrounds and provides a path from model discrimination toward measurement of the local velocity distribution.

## 27. [Beyond classification: regressing physical merger properties using solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14630) <a id="link27"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14630

**Authors:** Alex Brown, Georgios Exarchakis, Mathilda Avirett-Mackenzie, Carolin Villforth

**Abstract:** Galaxy mergers play an important role in galaxy evolution; they enhance star formation, transform morphologies, and may drive accretion onto black holes. Due to their complex morphological features, identification of mergers poses a significant challenge. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been successful at identifying mergers with good accuracy. However, similar to other deep learning techniques such as Vision Transformers, they require large training samples. Current methods are also limited to classification, rather than regression. Here, we apply the solid harmonic wavelet scattering bispectrum, a method that encodes invariances and symmetries in the data which need to be learned by CNNs, as an alternative to CNNs. We apply our methodology to a simulated dataset of galaxies with a wide range of merger properties. We show that this method outperforms standard methodologies, while requiring fewer training samples and being robust to noise. Most importantly, we show that for the first time this method is able to regress on both merger mass ratio and time since merger simultaneously, with uncertainties ~ 0.33 dex uncertainty in merger mass ratio and ~ 0.66 Gyr uncertainty in time since merger. We have therefore shown that solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum presents an alternative to currently used machine learning techniques.

## 28. [The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17224) <a id="link28"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17224

**Authors:** Marta Molero, Luca Boccioli, Almudena Arcones

**Abstract:** The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

## 29. [galpy with differentiable, accelerated backends: galactic dynamics in jax and PyTorch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14614) <a id="link29"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14614

**Authors:** Jo Bovy

**Abstract:** We describe an extension of galpy, the Python library for galactic dynamics, that adds jax and PyTorch as computational backends alongside its existing numpy and C implementation. With it, galpy's gravitational potentials, orbit integration, action-angle transformations and their inverses, and distribution functions, including those for tidal streams, run on GPUs, can be compiled as part of a user's program, and can be differentiated with respect to their inputs and parameters, from the force at a point to the samples drawn from a distribution function. The user-facing design is kept simple: the active backend follows from the type of the arrays that are passed in, the galpy interface is unchanged, and the numpy path gives the same results as before. We describe the design of the backend framework and its implementation in each of galpy's modules, with examples of use, and we discuss its limitations. On a GPU, batches of orbits, samples from distribution functions, and stream models run one to five orders of magnitude faster than on a single CPU core. To illustrate the new capabilities, we present simple examples of fitting the Galactic potential with a hypervelocity star and of learning the inverse action-angle transformation with a neural network trained through galpy. An AI coding agent wrote essentially all of the code under the detailed direction and review of the human author, and we describe how we organized this work and how we established the correctness of the result. This work is the start of galpy's version 2, which is available at https://github.com/jobovy/galpy and documented at https://docs.galpy.org/en/v2/ .

## 30. [Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17290) <a id="link30"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17290

**Authors:** William Lake, Paolo Padoan, {Å}ke Nordlund, Troels Haugb{ø}lle

**Abstract:** The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. This AMR-based method uses DISPATCH's local timestepping, allowing stellar environments and their larger scale cluster environments to step on separate timescales, and providing the framework needed to scale to long-duration simulations of GMCs. Direct radiation is transported in multiple bands, including both ionizing and nonionizing radiation, and uses short characteristics to maintain source directions and shadowing. Diffuse radiation is implemented for IR reprocessed light, with M1 and stationary ray options for transport. The thermochemical model includes atomic and molecular hydrogen and helium chemistry, and metal cooling and dust. It also includes a composition-dependent equation of state. Stellar masses grow through accretion of gas rather than a prescribed IMF, allowing stellar masses to respond to the evolving gas supply and feedback. In tests, multiple-source illumination retains geometric shadows while diffuse reprocessing heats shielded material, and tests of jets, ionization fronts, and radiation pressure demonstrate expected behavior and convergence. Ionization fronts also cross asynchronous refinement boundaries with late-time propagation speeds within a few percent of analytic predictions. Together, these developments provide a framework for determining how radiative and mechanical feedback modify the duration and efficiency of accretion from turbulent clouds, connecting the gas supply to individual stars with the high-mass stellar initial mass function.

## 31. [Diffuse interstellar bands in nearby galaxies with MaNGA: environmental trends with metallicity, extinction, ionization, and star-forming activity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15272) <a id="link31"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15272

**Authors:** Konstantinos Kouroumpatzakis, Santiago Jiménez, Boris Deshev, Richard Wünsch, Pavel Jáchym, Jan Cami, Jiří Kubát, Anežka Srbljanović

**Abstract:** Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are absorption features of uncertain origin observed in the optical and near-infrared spectra of stars and galaxies. Although their correlation with dust extinction is well established, the physical conditions governing their strength across different interstellar medium (ISM) environments remain poorly understood. We investigate the environmental dependence of the DIB $\lambda5780$ using spatially resolved MaNGA spectroscopy for 837 nearby galaxies spanning a broad range of stellar masses, star-formation rates, and ISM properties. Stellar and nebular parameters are derived via spectral fitting, while DIB absorption is measured from high-signal-to-noise spatially binned residual spectra. We detect the DIB $\lambda5780$ in 159 galaxies and report the most distant spatially resolved DIB detection to date, at 232 Mpc. The DIB $\lambda5780$ equivalent width correlates positively with both stellar and gas-phase extinction. DIB $\lambda5780$ is preferentially detected in regions of high extinction, near- or super-solar metallicity ($12+\log({\rm O/H})\gtrsim8.5$), and moderate specific star-formation rates ($-10.5\lesssim\log({\rm sSFR}/{\rm yr}^{-1})\lesssim-9$). By contrast, it falls below our detection threshold in metal-poor or strongly ionized environments. It is rarely detected in regions with little or no recent star formation, with the few detections in such environments occurring primarily in regions driven by composite ionization. Our results indicate that DIB $\lambda5780$ is preferentially detected, within the sensitivity limits of the MaNGA data, in dust-rich, chemically evolved, and moderately ionized environments.

## 33. [Machine-Learning Reconstruction of Intergalactic Medium Column-Density Maps from Observed Ly$\alpha$ Emission Cubes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16286) <a id="link33"></a>

**Abstract:** Understanding the large-scale structure of the intergalactic medium (IGM) is essential for studying galaxy evolution, particularly at $z \sim 2$--$6$, when cold filaments in the cosmic web are considered a primary mechanism for fueling galaxy growth. At these redshifts, Ly$\alpha$ emission shifts into the optical regime and serves as the primary tracer of diffuse IGM for ground-based integral field units (IFUs). However, detections remain limited by low signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) and the complexities of resonant scattering. We present a proof-of-concept machine-learning framework to reconstruct IGM gas column-density maps from noisy Ly$\alpha$ IFU emission cubes. The CDE successfully reconstructs broad filamentary structures in the simulated test set under these adopted assumptions. Applied to observed KCWI data, the CDE predicts gas column-density maps containing filamentary structures extending over $\gtrsim 40''$ ($\sim 1$ comoving Mpc), consistent with an IGM interpretation. The observed reconstructions remain conditional on the adopted models. These results illustrate the potential of the CDE framework for connecting diffuse Ly$\alpha$ observations with simulations of the IGM.

## 35. [AGB Atmospheres in Binary Environments: A First Step with CO5BOLB](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17125) <a id="link35"></a>

**Authors:** Gabriel Tomassini, Andrea Chiavassa, Bernd Freytag, Eric Lagadec

**Abstract:** Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars are characterized by complex atmospheric dynamics driven by convection and pulsations. In binary systems, the presence of a companion can further influence these dynamics, potentially affecting mass-loss processes and the morphology of the circumstellar environment, yet this influence on the atmosphere itself remains poorly quantified. This study aims to fill this gap by employing CO5BOLD simulations with a modified gravitational potential to explore how companion mass affects the atmospheric structure of AGB stars. We used radiative hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations with CO5BOLD to model the convective interior and atmosphere of AGB stars. We modified the gravitational potential to include a secondary mass and a centrifugal term, representing the companion as a point-mass potential on a steady, tidally locked circular orbit outside the computational domain, with the Coriolis force neglected. We performed simulations with different companion masses and using singular value decomposition (SVD), we identified the spatial distribution of pulsation energy and quantified its properties. We also examined the density structure to identify anisotropies induced by the companion. We isolate two dynamically distinct regimes, a pulsation-dominated layer and an outer, low-frequency outflow region, whose pulsation properties remain largely unaffected by the companion: their frequency, amplitude, and coherence stay consistent across all models. The density structure, by contrast, responds clearly to the companion, forming a pronounced anisotropy along the binary axis that strengthens with companion mass. This indicates that the intrinsic pulsational dynamics of the AGB star dominate over the tidal influence of the companion within the explored parameter space, while the density structure remains the most sensitive tracer of binarity.

**Abstract:** We demonstrate the capability of the slitless spectroscopic mode of the Euclid Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) to produce emission-line maps analogous to narrow-band images with user-defined central wavelengths. We present the first such maps of galaxies at $0.4 < z < 0.9$, constructed from blue-grism exposures obtained during the Euclid performance-verification observations of the Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field in November 2023. We demonstrate the use of these maps for identifying star-forming clumps, measuring radial star-formation profiles, detecting projected internal velocity gradients, deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex, and assessing spectroscopic redshift measurements. As a first statistical application, we reconstruct the galaxy mass--metallicity relation for 885 galaxies observed with the blue grism at $0.4 < z < 0.9$ by deblending the H$\alpha$--[N II] complex in the emission-line maps, and measure stacked H$\alpha$ radial profiles for 2634 galaxies over the same redshift range. The mass--metallicity relation is consistent with that obtained from the Euclid 1D spectroscopic measurements, demonstrating overall agreement between the two deblending approaches. The recovered H$\alpha$ radial profiles broadly follow the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ stellar continuum but remain modestly more extended after matching the $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ images to the H$\alpha$ PSF, consistent with previous results in the literature. Across the four $Y_{\mathrm{E}}$ size bins, we measure a mean $R_{50,\mathrm{H}\alpha}/R_{50,Y_{\mathrm{E}}}=1.15$.

## 38. [Identification of extragalactic radio sources in the VISTA survey of the Magellanic Clouds using an unsupervised machine learning algorithm](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15880) <a id="link38"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15880

**Authors:** Clara M. Pennock, Jacco Th. van Loon, Mohammed Iddrisu Nlowie, Elizabeth Joy Leese, Maja Nowaczyk, Heinz Andernach, Duncan Farrah, Valentin D. Ivanov, Micha{ł} J. Micha{ł}owski, Joana M. Oliveira, Jahang Prathap, Syed F. Rahman, Mara Salvato, Tayyaba Zafar

**Abstract:** The Magellanic Clouds benefit from a wealth of data across the electromagnetic spectrum, but extracting extragalactic sources from these crowded fields is a less than straightforward endeavour. We used an unsupervised machine learning algorithm (t-distributed stochastic neighbourhood embedding; t-SNE) to classify 6,652 and 1,356 sources in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, respectively, that were detected in the VISTA Survey of the Magellanic Clouds (VMC) and the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). Multi-wavelength photometry and colours from optical to radio were used as features to cluster similar sources together in 2D space on a t-SNE map. We used previously classified sources to separate the clusters into five classes: AGN, low-redshift galaxies, blazars, dusty stellar objects (e.g. young stellar objects, planetary nebul{\ae} etc) and high proper-motion stars. Previous photometric classifications from the literature match with specific clusters identified, as well as provide insight on areas of the t-SNE map for which there are no previous classifications. This work shows that the combination of unsupervised machine learning with photometry from optical to radio has proven adept at separating the stellar from the extragalactic, and the AGN from the galaxies. Our associated new spectroscopy with SALT includes new discoveries of AGN up to redshift 3.3 and Magellanic emission-line objects.

## 39. [Stellar Loci XI: Identifications and Parameter Determinations of Binary Stars by multi-band photometry](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16403) <a id="link39"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16403

**Authors:** Yuanchang Wang, Haibo Yuan, Zexi Niu, Kai Xiao, Bowen Huang, Ziqi Gao, Maosheng Xiang

**Abstract:** Large photometric surveys contain numerous unresolved binaries, but identifying them and measuring component properties remains challenging. We present a 65-band UV-to-IR SED-fitting framework to identify unresolved main-sequence binaries and infer their parameters. Photometry combines synthetic miniJPAS magnitudes from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra with 2MASS and WISE measurements. Using LAMOST-calibrated, metallicity-dependent stellar loci and a dwarf-star color-absolute-magnitude relation, we construct forward models for single stars and unresolved binaries. We fit both model families to each SED with MCMC, using Gaia distances as Hertzsprung-Russell-diagram constraints to infer metallicity, reddening, and component photometric parameters. Component masses and mass ratios are derived from PARSEC models. Simulations show the method robustly recovers binary parameters. Tests on a LAMOST comparison sample indicate sensitivity to binaries with $q\gtrsim0.4$; the preferred model reproduces spectroscopic metallicities with 0.11 dex scatter, while inferred reddenings agree with external extinction maps with $\sim0.02$ mag scatter. Comparison with an external Gaia XP-based binary catalog shows broadly consistent binary classifications for common sources. Our metallicities more closely follow the LAMOST spectroscopic scale, and mass-ratio estimates in the intermediate-$q$ regime better trace expected $\Delta$-HRD offsets. Tests using M67 members support internal consistency of inferred parameters. For quality-selected Gaia non-single-star binaries, primary-mass estimates agree with Gaia NSS values with 0.071 $M_\odot$ residual scatter; in cases with larger discrepancies, further tests indicate that secondary-mass and mass-ratio estimates are more reliable than the Gaia NSS values. The method scales to large photometric samples, enabling population studies and analyses of individual systems.

**Novelty:** 5

## 40. [Automated identification of dipole mixed-modes in red-giant stars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15882) <a id="link40"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15882

**Authors:** Francisca Espinoza-Rojas, Michaël Bazot, Saskia Hekker, Sébastien Bourguignon

**Abstract:** Dipole mixed modes probe the internal structure of red giants by carrying information from both the convective envelope and the radiative core. Hence, identifying these modes allows for the determination of evolutionary states and stellar interior conditions. This identification typically relies on comparing observed frequencies with theoretical ones derived from the mixed-mode asymptotic relation. However, the process is challenging due to parameter-space degeneracies, stellar rotation, as well as missing modes and spurious peaks in the power density spectrum. In this work, we aim to develop an automated method for identifying dipole mixed modes, suitable for large-scale asteroseismic analyses. We introduce a metric that measures the overlap between observed and asymptotic dipole frequencies, represented as spike trains convolved with Gaussian kernels. After optimising this metric with a genetic algorithm, we use the best-fit parameters to perform a global assignment of the oscillation modes. We then validated the method using synthetic frequencies of RGB and CHeB stars perturbed by stellar rotation, and further tested it on four benchmark stars. Validation using perturbed synthetic frequencies shows that our method recovers over 95% of the dipole mixed modes across different evolutionary states, and this performance remains robust to spurious peaks and missing modes. For the benchmark stars, our dipole mode identification is consistent with previously published results, with mixed-mode parameter estimates typically agreeing within 1% for ${\Delta}{\Pi}$1 and 10% for ${\delta}{\nu}$rot and $q$. Our analysis demonstrates that the proposed method effectively addresses the challenges associated with the complex dipole mode spectrum. Thus, it enables automated identification of dipole mixed modes, supporting homogeneous, large-scale asteroseismic analyses of evolved stars.

**Novelty:** 5

## 41. [Estimating distances from parallaxes. VII. Computing the three-dimensional kinegeometric posterior with one-dimensional sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17231) <a id="link41"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17231

**Authors:** Coryn A. L. Bailer-Jones

**Abstract:** When parallaxes are of poor quality, proper motions can improve stellar distance estimates using known constraints on stars' physical velocities. Formally this may be achieved via the kinegeometric posterior, a three-dimensional (3D) posterior in distance and velocity for given measured parallax and 2D proper motion. This posterior is the product of a covariant Gaussian likelihood in the parallax and proper motion with a distance and velocity prior that can be constructed from a Galaxy model. In earlier work, I showed how to infer this posterior for stars in Gaia DR3 by explicitly sampling it with a Markov Chain Monte Carlo method. Here I show that this posterior is equivalent to a 1D posterior in distance combined with a sum of 2D Gaussian distributions in velocity. This 1D+2D representation is both faster and more accurate to sample, thereby making the computation of the kinegeometric posterior for a large set of sources much easier.

**Novelty:** 5

## 42. [3D dust attenuation effects in galaxies: structural biases and induced negative color gradients](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15355) <a id="link42"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15355

**Authors:** João Duarte, Santiago González-Gaitán, Polychronis Papaderos, Ana M. Mourão, Rita P. Santos

**Abstract:** Radial surface brightness profiles (SBPs) and color gradients are useful tools for studying galaxy structure, formation, and evolution. While it is usually assumed that they are primarily driven by stellar properties, such as mass, age or metallicity, their dependence on 3D dust attenuation is not fully understood or accounted for. We analyze how 3D dust attenuation affects galaxy observations by hindering the estimation of intrinsic properties. We examine dust-induced shifts in surface brightness and color. Using SKIRT radiative transfer models, we simulated simple S\'ersic galaxies, with spherically-symmetric stellar densities, constant stellar-to-dust ratios, and a spatially constant spectral energy distribution (SED). We find that attenuated SBPs differ significantly from dust-free profiles, particularly in the central galaxy regions. These differences become more pronounced at bluer wavelengths and for higher core dust densities, leading to variations in the fitted S\'ersic index of up to ~25%. This can lead to incorrect conclusions about the intrinsic stellar distribution and mimic a central mass deficit. For galaxies with very centrally-dense dust distributions, a core-S\'ersic model results in a better fit of the attenuated SBP. For dust masses as low as ~2*10^6 $M_{\odot}$, dust-induced negative color gradients reach the same order of magnitude as those commonly observed in galaxies, which a dust-screen fails to account for. This occurs even for a spatially invariant SED and can lead to wrong conclusions about intrinsic stellar populations and related astrophysical questions, such as their formation histories or the mechanisms of inside-out star formation quenching. A full 3D approach is necessary to properly model attenuation effects, which, if not accounted for, can bias inferences made about stellar populations, their evolutionary histories, and spatial distributions.

**Relevance:** 3
**Novelty:** 5

**Abstract:** Understanding the intrinsic 3D shapes of galaxies provides crucial insights into their formation and evolution, but determining these from projections remains challenging. We apply a Bayesian inference framework to optical images of galaxies from the Euclid Data Release 1, leveraging its large sample size to test the scalability and robustness of this methodology. Applying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling to S\'ersic axis ratios and effective radii, we constrain the population-level mean 3D ellipticity, triaxiality, and size, together with their covariances for $40\,864\,304$ star-forming galaxies with stellar masses $M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{10.5}M_\odot$ at redshifts $0<1.2$. Our sample size exceeds previous shape inference studies by factors of $440$--$52\,800$ relative to early observations by JWST, and factors of $440$--$17\,600$ relative to legacy observations from HST in overlapping mass-redshift bins, enabling finer binning alongside improved statistical constraints on shape evolution. We additionally include over 9 million galaxies at $z<0.5$, a regime historically limited by sample size in previous shape inference studies. We recover key evolutionary trends identified in previous smaller-sample studies. We find high ellipticities ($\mu_E \sim 0.600$--$0.821$) across all bins, indicating that the underlying 3D shape distributions are statistically dominated by flattened geometries. Most notably, we recover the decline of the prolate fraction towards $z=0$ at low masses ($M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{9.5}M_\odot$) reported by previous studies. This trend is seen consistently in comparable analyses of independent data sets spanning different depths and resolution regimes, showing that it is not an artefact of small-sample statistics, suggesting it may be a genuine feature of galaxy evolution. We also identify future methodological improvements for subsequent Euclid data releases.

**Relevance:** 3
**Novelty:** 5

## 44. [Cosmic Ray Reacceleration and Gamma-Ray Emission via the Cloud-Wind Interaction in the Galactic Halo](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15120) <a id="link44"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15120

**Authors:** Ryohei Inamoto, Jiro Shimoda, Katsuaki Asano

**Abstract:** The interaction between cosmic rays (CRs) and multiphase gas in the Galactic halo may play an important role in shaping the hard gamma-ray spectrum of the Fermi bubbles. We investigate the interaction between a hot Galactic wind and a cold, dense gas clump with a relative velocity of $300\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$ using two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations coupled with momentum-dependent CR transport. The system produces a bow shock and wind reacceleration region downstream, where the wind flow is faster than the initial velocity. For a CR pressure comparable to the gas pressure (CR-rich), the wind acceleration and turbulence behind the clump are enhanced. When CR pressure is dynamically weak, strong gas compression leads to significant CR spectral hardening. In contrast, for the CR-rich case, CR pressure gradients weaken the gas compression and suppress further CR reacceleration. We estimate the gamma-ray intensity from CRs, and find that reaccelerated CRs penetrate the dense clump and enhance hadronic gamma-ray emission. The gamma-ray intensity reaches $\sim 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,sr^{-1}}$ in the 1--10 GeV band, and the gamma-ray spectra become significantly harder, consistent with the Fermi bubbles' emission. These results suggest that an ensemble of dense gas clumps interacting with the Galactic wind may contribute to the gamma-ray emission of the Fermi bubbles.

**Relevance:** 3
**Novelty:** 5

## 45. [UOCS. XVI. Census of post mass-transfer binaries across various evolutionary phases in M67](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15230) <a id="link45"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15230

**Authors:** Harshit Pal, Vikrant V. Jadhav, Arumalla B. S. Reddy, Annapurni Subramaniam

**Abstract:** M67 is a well-studied, solar-metallicity, old open cluster that hosts a diverse set of exotic stellar populations formed via mass transfer (MT). While Case A, B, and C MT systems have been individually examined in several clusters, a comprehensive investigation of all MT types across different evolutionary stages within a single cluster remains limited. This study aims to detect the presence of post mass-transfer systems using two different methods and thereby obtain a holistic view of binary evolution and mass-transfer mechanisms prevalent in M67. We constructed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) for 141 UV-detected stars in M67 using far-UV data from AstroSat/UVIT, combined with archival data from Swift/UVOT, GALEX, Gaia, 2MASS, WISE, and other sources. Furthermore, we performed a detailed chemical abundance analysis of cluster members using high-resolution spectroscopy from the GALAH DR3+ survey. We identified 11 new MS+WD binaries with previously undetected hotter companions, effectively doubling the known MS+WD binary population in M67. This includes five confirmed ELM WDs with orbital periods of 100-200 days and no chemical peculiarities, confirming Case A or B post-MT systems. We also detected 13 long-period SB1 systems with orbital periods longer than 1000 days and enhancements in s-process elements (Ba, La, Y), indicating Case C post-MT systems enriched by thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (AGB) companions which have evolved into undetected WDs. This study demonstrates that M67 hosts a diverse population of post-mass transfer binaries formed via Case A, B, and C mechanisms. The unified view makes M67 a key benchmark for studying binary star evolution and highlights the role of UV observations and high-resolution spectroscopy in uncovering hidden stellar histories.

**Relevance:** 3
**Novelty:** 5

Crill (Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, 4800 Oak Grove Drive, Pasadena, CA, 91109, USA), D. Scott (Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1, Canada)

**Abstract:** Accurate photometric-redshift estimation and calibration of the weak-lensing point-spread function (PSF) for Euclid require complementary ground-based optical imaging with high photometric precision and spatial homogeneity. The Organisation Unit for External Data (OU-EXT) integrates heterogeneous ground-based surveys into the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), delivering uniformly calibrated, co-added images, and associated PSF models. To minimise systematics in spectral energy distribution (SED) reconstruction and photometric-redshift estimation, these data must achieve relative photometric stability at the $\sim$10 mmag level on Euclid-tile scales. We present the ground-based imaging component of Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), comprising $\sim2500$ deg$^2$ across the wide, deep, and auxiliary fields. We summarise the OU-EXT production workflow and validation framework, and quantify the achieved data quality of the co-added products in terms of depth, photometric zero-point stability, and spatial colour homogeneity. In the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS), the point-source $10\sigma$ depths in the $griz$ bands reach 24.8/24.3/24.0/23.0 AB mag, with the deep fields extending 1--2 magnitudes deeper. Most EWS DR1 tiles meet the 10 mmag relative photometric requirement, with 1.1% and 1.5% showing offsets exceeding 50 mmag in the northern and southern hemispheres, respectively. Spatial colour variations remain typically below 5--10 mmag across the southern EWS footprint, while larger residual structures of 10--25 mmag appear in some northern regions. These results demonstrate that the EXT production chain provides a largely homogeneous framework for integrating ground-based datasets into Euclid, while identifying calibration and co-addition limitations that have to be addressed in DR2 to meet the mission's most stringent cosmological requirements. (Abridged)

## 47. [Starspots on eclipsing giant stars II.: TESS continuous viewing zone giant V521 Dra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17080) <a id="link47"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17080

**Authors:** A. Haris, B. Seli, K. Oláh, S. Rappaport, J. S. Thomsen, M. Turkki, T. Hackman, M. Tuomi, K. Yakut, A. Casasbuenas, M. A. Díaz, J. H. Terwel, B. N. Hauptmann, R. Gagliano, T. L. Jacobs, M. H. Kristiansen, H. M. Schwengeler, M. Omohundro, I. Terentev, B. Powell, V. Kostov, Zs. Kővári

**Abstract:** Eclipsing binaries are exceptional laboratories for stellar astrophysics. By analysing the modulations in their eclipse light curves, we can probe their surface inhomogeneities. The eclipse-mapping technique enables us to scan starspots in detail, using the transit of a companion star across the surface of a spotted star. When multiple consecutive eclipses are observed, this method may also reveal the evolution of spot properties and provide evidence for stellar differential rotation. We study the magnetic activity of V521 Dra, a tidally locked eclipsing binary with a red giant primary and a main-sequence secondary, both of K spectral class, on a 4.27 d orbit. This is an exceptional system with ~5.3 years of TESS 2 min cadence observations. This offers a unique opportunity to study magnetic activity in uninterrupted blocks over several years with very high photometric precision. We aim to constrain the evolution of the spot pattern of V521 Dra A. We used two methods to study the spot activity of the primary: eclipse mapping and analytic spot modelling. We analysed the stellar properties of the system with a set of methods, including combined modelling of the eclipse light curves, radial velocity data, spectral energy distribution analysis, and forward modelling of the whole orbital light curve. The star shows strong spot-induced modulations both in the eclipse and out-of-eclipse parts of the light curve. We identified 540 spot eclipse signals in 203 primary eclipses. Eclipse mapping reveals the presence of up to four spots. The spot longitudes drift continuously in time, indicating differential rotation. Spots in the eclipse-mapping data show differing angular velocities in their drift, implying a near-surface shear in the convective zone of the primary. Using time series spectroscopy and the spectral energy distribution, we constrained the astrophysical parameters of the binary system.

## 48. [Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS): the Outflow-Luminosity Scaling Relations in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16830) <a id="link48"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16830

**Authors:** Suinan Zhang, Kei E. I. Tanaka, Yichen Zhang, Takashi Shimonishi, Yu Cheng, Kenji Furuya, Asako Sato

**Abstract:** Understanding massive star formation in low-metallicity environments is crucial for constraining the universality of star formation across cosmic evolution. In this Letter, we present the first systematic survey of massive protostellar outflows in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC, $Z\sim$0.2--0.5 $Z_\odot$), as part of the Magellanic Outflow and Chemistry Survey (MAGOS). MAGOS targets 40 massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) with luminosities of (1--23)$\times 10^4$ $L_\odot$ with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 0.85 mm at a linear resolution of $\sim$0.1 pc. Using CO (3--2), we identify blue- and red-shifted outflows associated with the primary continuum sources toward 29 targets in the LMC and 10 targets in the SMC. Comparing the outflow mass, momentum, energy, and force versus luminosity scaling relations in MAGOS with those in the Galaxy, we find that the LMC CO outflows have a similar slope in the mass-luminosity relation, suggesting that CO remains an effective tracer of massive protostellar outflows at $Z\sim$0.5 $Z_\odot$. In contrast, despite the large scatter, the SMC CO outflows are deficient at high luminosity and show flatter scaling relations than the LMC and the Galaxy. This is consistent with reduced CO abundances due to enhanced photodissociation at high luminosity and low metallicity ($Z\sim$0.2 $Z_\odot$), although the possibility of intrinsically weak outflow launching cannot be ruled out with the current data.

R. Weaver (MIT Kavli Institute for Astrophysics and Space Research, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA 02139, USA), A. H. Wright (Ruhr University Bochum, Faculty of Physics and Astronomy, Astronomical Institute)

**Abstract:** Euclid is a European Space Agency mission mapping the extragalactic sky, aiming to provide the most-accurate 3D view of the Universe at optical and near-infrared wavelengths, by measuring the photometric redshifts of billions of galaxies. Within the Euclid Consortium, this task is executed by the PHZ Organisation Unit. PHZ takes as input the multi-wavelength photometry of Euclid and ground-based data, and returns as output the source classification, photometric redshifts for the Euclid core science (i.e., cosmology), and photometric redshifts plus physical parameters and absolute magnitudes for non-cosmological science. As part of the first Euclid Data Release (DR1), we describe the details of the DR1 pipeline for non-cosmological science, along with the released data products, and their validation. The non-cosmological science data products are obtained with NNPZ, a nearest-neighbour algorithm developed within PHZ that infers the properties of each target galaxy from its closest matches, in colour-magnitude space, within a reference sample of galaxies with known redshifts and physical parameters. We built this reference sample from Euclid observations of COSMOS, one of the Euclid Auxiliary Fields, labelling each galaxy with redshifts and physical parameters derived from the COSMOS2020 multi-wavelength photometry, consistently with the Euclid core-science results. Combined with the adjustments and priors required to generalise the results across the entire extragalactic sky, this approach yields high-quality and internally consistent data products. We tested the performance using both internal metrics and comparisons to ancillary data sets (e.g., COSMOS2020, 3D-HST, and DESI) and scaling relations (e.g., the star-forming main sequence); the results are in line with expectations and pre-DR1 simulations for both the Euclid Wide Survey and Euclid Deep Fields.

**Relevance:** 3
**Novelty:** 5

## 50. [Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14998) <a id="link50"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14998

**Authors:** Xinlin Zhao, Song Wang, Guang-Yao Xiao, Meng Sun, Roberto Soria, Kyle Akira Rocha, Seth Goggage, Pengfei Wang, Hongliang Yan, Xuan Mao, Yang Huang, Maosheng Xiang, Shuai Liu, Dan Qiu, Meng Zhang, Xue Li, Fabo Feng, Xihong Luo, Xiaohong Yang, Jifeng Liu

**Abstract:** Supermassive neutron stars ($M \gtrsim 2\ M_{\odot}$) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period $P\approx 1218\pm3$ days and a comparatively low eccentricity $e\approx 0.09\pm0.01$ (with $1 \sigma$ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from {\it Gaia} DR2 and DR3 catalogues, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle $i\approx73^{\circ}\pm11^{\circ}$. The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8--2.8 $M_{\odot}$ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of $2.20^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ $M_{\odot}$. This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 7

## 51. [$uvby-\beta$ photoelectric photometry of FGK-type pulsating star candidates in the Kepler field: observations, stellar parameters and asteroseismic analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15907) <a id="link51"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15907

**Authors:** L. Fox-Machado

**Abstract:** We present $uvby-\beta$ photoelectric photometry of 218 FGK-type stars brighter than $Kp = 12$ mag in the Kepler field. Interstellar reddening was estimated using the observed photometric indices, distances from Gaia DR3, and the Bayestar19 three-dimensional dust maps. The sample was classified into dwarf and giant stars, and their metallicities and effective temperatures were determined using empirical photometric calibrations. The resulting parameters were compared with those reported in previous photometric and spectroscopic studies. We also analyzed the Kepler long-cadence light curves of the sample and determined the global asteroseismic parameters, including the frequency of maximum oscillation power ($\nu_{\max}$) and the large frequency separation ($\Delta\nu$), for red giants exhibiting solar-like oscillations. Finally, we performed a Bayesian isochrone-fitting analysis using PARSEC stellar evolutionary models, incorporating the photometric metallicities and effective temperatures, the asteroseismic parameters, and absolute visual magnitudes derived from Gaia DR3 data as observational constraints. This analysis provides estimates of the fundamental stellar parameters, including effective temperatures, metallicities, surface gravities, masses, and radii, together with their associated uncertainties.

**Relevance:** 3
**Novelty:** 4

Scott (Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1, Canada)

**Abstract:** We present 15 072 high-confidence strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), spanning 2000 deg$^2$. These comprise 6073 grade A ('sure lens') and 8999 grade B ('probable lens') systems, which we publish alongside a further 9010 grade C ('possible lens') candidates. With more high-confidence candidates than all previous catalogues combined, this sample establishes a large, homogeneous data set of galaxy-scale strong lenses with high-resolution imaging, transforming strong lensing from a field of rare discoveries to a robust statistical tool for astrophysics and cosmology. Of the roughly 900 million sources in DR1, we searched the 68 million passing our catalogue selection using a bespoke discovery pipeline that synthesises scores from five machine-learning models with visual classifications from around 7000 citizen scientists and 67 strong lensing experts. Beyond classical Einstein rings, our catalogue includes 84 candidate double-source-plane lenses and over 1000 candidate disc lenses, two exotic classes with few previously known examples, as well as several hundred candidate lensed AGN and quasars. We deliver automated lens models for the combined grade A+B systems, and photometric redshifts and stellar population properties for the deflector galaxies, providing immediate science-ready data products. We find that the majority of the deflector galaxies are massive and quiescent, with stellar masses of $\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$ (Salpeter initial mass function; 16th-84th percentile range). The deflector galaxies span a range of photometric redshifts ($z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$), extending to higher redshifts than previous ground-based lens samples, and the lenses have a typical Einstein radius of $0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec. Extrapolating by area, we expect over 100 000 high-confidence strong lens candidates in the Euclid Wide Survey.

**Novelty:** 6

## 53. [Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14703) <a id="link53"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14703

**Authors:** Lael Shin, Daniel Apai, Yifan Zhou, Joshua D. Lothringer, Daphne Broski-Laing, Sarah L. Casewell, Siyi Xu, Ben W. P. Lew, Xianyu Tan, Jenni R. French, Vivien Parmentier, Mark S. Marley, L. C. Mayorga

**Abstract:** We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching ~280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to ~3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 6

H. Wright (Ruhr University Bochum, Faculty of Physics and Astronomy, Astronomical Institute)

**Abstract:** We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.

## 55. [ViViViT: a Video-to-Video Vision Transformer for Cosmological Lightcone Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14617) <a id="link55"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14617

**Authors:** Federico Semenzato, Alvise Raccanelli, Michele Liguori

**Abstract:** Moving along the line of sight of a cosmological lightcone also moves through cosmic time, as in a video of cosmic structure traced by an evolving observable. We recast the reconstruction of the underlying matter field from observed lightcones as a video-to-video translation task by introducing ViViViT, a vision transformer that factorizes attention across transverse frames and radial evolution. On reconstructed matter fields from 21cm neutral hydrogen simulations over $z\in[7.66,16.00]$, ViViViT preserves spectral power and phase alignment within a few percent of the ground truth up to the Nyquist scale, and three-point correlations for all triangle configurations with sides up to $k\simeq0.77\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$, outperforming a convolutional 3D-U-Net baseline across all measured statistics. By encoding the evolving geometry of the cosmological observable itself, ViViViT marks a step toward field-level architectures that natively respect cosmic time, opening the path to time-aware reconstruction of cosmic tracers and targeted searches for redshift-dependent signatures in 21cm data.

**Novelty:** 6

## 56. [Sailing with the winds of HL Tau: the JWST view](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15910) <a id="link56"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15910

**Authors:** T. Nony, F. Bacciotti, C. Dougados, M. G. Navarro, B. Nisini, P. Kavanagh, A. Banzatti, V. Delabrosse, L. Podio, S. Cabrit, A. Caratti o Garatti, D. Coffey, T. P. Ray, F. Massi, D. Fedele, E. Whelan, A. Garufi, S. Antoniucci

**Abstract:** Studying protostellar ejections is crucial to understanding the formation of young stars and planetary systems. The Class I/II star HL Tau, with its ringed disk and prominent bipolar outflows, is a benchmark system for these studies. We provide a first overview of our Cycle 3 JWST program targeting HL Tau, focusing on the morphology and kinematics of the various wind components as well as on the water emission lines excited in the inner disk. Our observations cover the 1.66-28 $\mu$m spectral range, combining NIRSpec and MIRI MRS mosaics to map the inner 10" of the red-shifted lobe of the outflow and the base of the blue-shifted lobe. In the red-shifted lobe we observe a stratified wind of three nested layers: a fast, highly collimated atomic jet structured in a chain of eight knots and with radial velocities of 160 km/s; a wide-angle H$_2$ wind with velocities of 45 km/s exhibiting complex arc-like substructures; and a warm gas shell, of radial velocity of 35 km/s, visible in low-excitation transitions of CO ($\nu$=1-0). This CO shell appears co-spatial with the CO (J=2-1) emission detected by ALMA with velocities from 3 to 25 km/s. In the first 1" of the blue-shifted lobe we detect a similar stratification, but the jet is faster and less collimated. The observed stratification and kinematics of the flow may support a magnetically driven disk-wind scenario in which the distinct components originate in the disk at progressively larger distances from the star. However, while the external components observed in CO have the laminar and regular appearance predicted for such winds, the knots in the inner jet and the arcs in the wind could be the manifestation of a pulsed ejection mechanism. Additionally, in MIRI spectra taken at the star position we detect a forest of water lines dominated by cold-to-warm (< 500 K) gas. Their distribution suggests an extended reservoir of sublimated ices.

## 57. [Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$\alpha$ Forest at the Field Level](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17299) <a id="link57"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17299

**Authors:** Divij Sharma, Roger de Belsunce, Mikhail M. Ivanov

**Abstract:** We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Ly-alpha) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.

**Abstract:** We present the pipeline design of the photometric redshift processing function for Data Release 1 (DR1) of the $Euclid$ mission, and the validation and performance of our cosmology-related products that are released as part of DR1-Foundation. The $Euclid$ mission aims to constrain the equation-of-state parameter of dark energy, $w$, to percent-level accuracy through the measurement of large-scale structure via weak gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering. As part of DR1-Foundation we release determinations of photometric redshifts (photo-$z$), corrected photometry, and object classes that are used to form the basis of the cosmological samples. The release furthermore includes estimates of the spectral energy distributions of stars and galaxies for the careful modelling of the point-spread function for weak-lensing measurement. We estimate the performance of the photo-$z$ point estimates and probability distribution functions using overlapping spectroscopic redshifts, which are weighted to match different flux-limited target samples. We find that the current performance is somewhat below mission design requirements ($40\%$ in scatter and a factor of 2 in outlier fraction) at the nominal survey depth ($I_{\rm E}<24.5$), but closely matching requirements at slightly brighter magnitudes ($I_{\rm E}<24$), consistent with pre-launch analyses and the slightly shallower external data (up to $0.3\,\mathrm{mag}$) with respect to end-of-mission expectations. Data from Rubin-LSST will help alleviate this issue by the time of the final cosmology analyses. The other cosmology-related outputs are tested to the extent that is possible with currently available comparison data. This paper is partnered by an article describing the measurement of the physical properties of galaxies for the purpose of non-cosmological science.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 5
