## 59. [From $3\times2$pt to $4\times3$pt: calibrating galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments with galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15471) <a id="link59"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15471

**Authors:** Raphaël Kou, Antony Lewis

**Abstract:** Combining galaxy clustering and weak gravitational lensing beyond two-point statistics offers a way to extract additional cosmological information while calibrating astrophysical nuisance parameters. We investigate this approach by combining 1-loop power spectra with tree-level bispectra, including all auto- and cross-bispectra of galaxy clustering and weak lensing, a combination that we refer to as $4\times3$pt by analogy with the well-known $3\times2$pt analysis. Modelling two- and three-point statistics consistently, with galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments described by the TATT model, we perform Fisher forecasts of dark energy constraints for a Euclid-like survey, with conservative scale cuts. When combined with CMB data, adding $4\times3$pt bispectra to the $3\times2$pt improves the dark energy figure of merit by about $30\%$, a gain that remains stable when using the three, four or five lowest redshift bins of our ten. To extend the analysis to ten tomographic bins, we compress the bispectra into skew-spectra, which improve the figure of merit by $20\%$ with the CMB and by $37\%$ without. We show that most of this improvement comes from the calibration of second-order galaxy bias parameters by three-point statistics, mainly by the galaxy-auto and the GGL bispectra. We also find that baryonic feedback is correlated with second-order intrinsic alignment parameters once the amplitude of the matter power spectrum is constrained by the CMB, and that bispectra reduce this correlation by calibrating intrinsic alignments, almost entirely through the GGL bispectra, a mechanism that could become more valuable with more flexible baryonic feedback models. These results demonstrate the potential of combined galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra to improve cosmological constraints from stage-IV galaxy surveys through the calibration of galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments.

**Novelty:** 5

## 60. [Localization of gravitational-wave source behind galaxy clusters by gravitational-wave lensing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16916) <a id="link60"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16916

**Authors:** Brian H. Y. Cheng, Laura Uronen, Souvik Jana, Samuel Lange, Thomas E. Collett, Otto A. Hannuksela

**Abstract:** Gravitational-wave observations have opened new opportunities to study massive object events like merging binary black holes. When combined with electromagnetic counterparts, accurate localization of gravitational-wave sources could allow us to identify their host galaxies and carry out follow-up studies, such as study the environment of merging black holes and determine the Hubble constant. One of the possible methods for precise localization is strong gravitational-wave lensing. Previous studies have considered strong gravitational-wave lensing with galaxy lenses. However, galaxy clusters have yet to be investigated due to the complexity of their mass structures. Here we take the list of known cluster lenses from the Hubble Frontier Fields, simulate lensing properties of gravitational waves from their reconstructions as they would be observed by the ground-based gravitational-wave detectors. When same model family is used in simulation and localization, we find that the correct lens is identified for around 90\% of the simulated events. We also show that the source positions within the cluster can be pinpointed at sub-arcsecond precision with an estimate on source redshift. When we marginalize over all possible lens models for the clusters, the lens identification and localizations remain valid as long as the correct lens model is contained in the available cluster lens models. However, most localization attempts fail at initialization if the correct cluster model is excluded. These tests establish a proof of concept of localization under idealized conditions, while more work is needed to understand the cluster lens modeling discrepancies and reconstruction bias to validate the approach further.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 5

## 61. [MAHA-z: A Mahalanobis distance kNN estimator for photometric redshifts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14582) <a id="link61"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14582

**Authors:** Paula S. Ferreira, Ribamar R. R. Reis, Renyue Cen

**Abstract:** We present \texttt{MAHA-z}, a photometric-redshift (photo-$z$) estimator that combines $k$-nearest neighbour ($k$NN) regression with a Mahalanobis distance metric learned from the covariance of a spectroscopic reference sample. For each target galaxy, \texttt{MAHA-z} performs a neighbour search in a colour-magnitude feature space with optional morphological parameters, and returns both a point estimate and a redshift posterior $p(z\mid\mathbf{f})$ obtained by kernel density estimation over the neighbour redshifts. The Mahalanobis metric accounts for correlated features and heterogeneous units, eliminating ad hoc normalisation, and its subspace restriction allows \texttt{MAHA-z} to handle missing bands on a per-galaxy basis without imputation. We validate the method on four datasets spanning simulations and survey photometry: the Euclid Flagship~2 mock, the Legacy-KiDZ calibration sample, VIPERS, and the DES Year~3 BAO sample. On Euclid Flagship~2 (LSST+NISP) we achieve $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}=0.0148$ with a $0.27\%$ outlier fraction, and on DES Y3 we obtain $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}\approx0.023$ with $<1\%$ outliers and posterior calibration comparable to the \texttt{ANNz2} catalogue. \texttt{MAHA-z} processes millions of galaxies in minutes and provides competitive PDFs at substantially lower computational cost than trained machine-learning models, making it a practical option for iterative photo-$z$ production and validation in Stage-IV surveys.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 5

## 62. [A new indirect approach for oxygen abundance determinations across a wide range of physical conditions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15581) <a id="link62"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15581

**Authors:** Sandra Zamora, Asier Castrillo, A. I. Díaz, Marta Gavilán

**Abstract:** In this work we present a new approach to derive HII region metal abundances based on sulfur emission lines. We select M101 as benchmark galaxy to test our new methodology along the wide metallicity gradient of this huge face-on star-forming spiral. Based on previous studies, we compile a sample of 151 HII regions and compare their properties base on the galaxy radial profile. The new methodology is based on the derivation of the electron temperature of the double ionised sulfur, either by the direct measurement of the [SIII] auroral line or, at supersolar metalicities, from the $SO_{23}$ parameter. This new indirect method is able to extend the abundance gradient up to the very centre of the M101 galaxy (0.04 $R_e$). This new methodology mitigates systematic biases in direct abundance determinations based on auroral lines, while opening up new opportunities to improve commonly used strong line abundance calibrations in the intermediate to high metallicity regime.

## 63. [Low effective-temperature diminution of H$\alpha$ emission from metallic centrifugal magnetospheres fed by ion-runaway winds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15352) <a id="link63"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15352

**Authors:** Stanley P. Owocki, Jiri Krticka, M. E. Shultz, Asif ud-Doula

**Abstract:** Main-sequence B-stars with a strong magnetic field and moderately rapid rotation form centrifugal magnetospheres (CMs), which often exhibit distinct H$\alpha$ line emission, as well as circularly polarized radio. For CMs of early-type B-stars with $T_{\rm eff} \gtrsim 17$ kK, the onset and strength of the H$\alpha$ emission is well explained in terms of a centrifugal breakout (CBO) model, in which mass fed into the CM by the star's radiatively driven stellar wind builds up to a density that is sufficient for centrifugal forces to overwhelm magnetic confinement. The analysis here now argues that the observed diminution and disappearance of the H$\alpha$ emission for CM B-stars with $T_{\rm eff} \lesssim 17$ kK can be explained by the failure of their lower luminosity to drive hydrogen-rich winds; instead they develop an ion runaway of heavier metal ions that are the seat of line-driving, which thus feed a metallic CM (mCM) for which the requisite hydrogen is diminished or even absent. For mid-B-type stars in a narrow transition range of effective temperature $T_{\rm eff} \approx (16.8 \pm 0.3)$ kK, hydrogen can still be driven to a sufficient speed to coast into the inner CM, which we show can explain the reduced strength and width of H$\alpha$ line emission in the transition CM star $\rho$ Oph C. But even in regions with no hydrogen, the build-up of metal density to CBO levels can still drive the magnetic reconnection needed to produce the observed radio. We discuss whether such build-up of metals could give rise to direct observational signatures.

**Novelty:** 5

## 64. [FastBox: A lightweight Python package for rapid cosmological 21cm intensity mapping simulations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15906) <a id="link64"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15906

**Authors:** Philip Bull, Bruno B. Bizarria, Melis O. Irfan, Geoff Murphy

**Abstract:** FastBox is a Python package for generating fast, physically realistic simulations of cosmological signals in three-dimensional co-moving boxes, with the primary focus of its application being 21cm intensity mapping (IM) experiments. It provides a framework for producing cosmology-dependent Gaussian and log-normal density fields, as well as modelling the effects of redshift-space distortions and linear biasing, among others. Models of instrumental systematics are incorporated, including radiometer noise and beam convolutions. Diffuse and point source foreground models are included, along with a number of foreground filtering strategies such as PCA, ICA, and transfer function correction via mock signal injection. Lastly, estimators are provided for power spectra, the two-point correlation function, and the equilateral bispectrum. The same underlying density field can also be Poisson-sampled into a discrete galaxy catalogue, so that 21cm and galaxy tracers are simulated from common initial conditions and their cross-power spectrum can be measured. Simulation grids may be cubic or anisotropic, with independent side lengths and cell counts along each Cartesian axis. FastBox is designed as a lightweight but realistic test-bench for the development and validation of end-to-end cosmological analysis pipelines.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 5

Yeung (Institute for Astronomy, University of Edinburgh, Royal Observatory, Blackford Hill, Edinburgh EH9 3HJ, UK), D. Scott (Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1, Canada)

**Abstract:** Applications of strong gravitational lensing in astrophysics and cosmology critically depend on building reliable strong lensing models, which require accurate measurements of on-sky positions of multiple images and of the redshifts of the background sources from which they originate. In this context, Euclid is a unique facility, as it simultaneously provides high-resolution multi-band photometric imaging and slitless spectroscopy for an unprecedentedly large sample of gravitational lenses, most of which are newly discovered. In this work, we exploit Euclid slitless spectroscopic data to determine the redshifts of four spatially extended lensed sources, and to reconstruct emission-line images. Specifically, two of the target sources are lensed into giant arcs by the massive galaxy clusters SPT-CLJ0411$-$4819 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.424$, where "d" denotes the lensing deflector) and Abell 2280 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.326$). The third system is a quadruply imaged active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidate strongly lensed by a massive galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.68$, while the fourth is a galaxy-scale Einstein ring produced by a lens galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.235$. This work represents a proof of concept for the exploitation of Euclid slitless spectroscopic data in the study of strong gravitational lensing, providing one of the first determinations of spectroscopic redshifts for strongly lensed features from NISP spectra. These results demonstrate the feasibility of applying the same methodology to the very large sample of gravitational lenses that Euclid has started to discover and is expected to identify over the course of the mission.

## 66. [The Same But Different: SiO$_2$ Clouds in Two L-Dwarfs with JWST](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16783) <a id="link66"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16783

**Authors:** Joshua D. Lothringer, Jeff A. Valenti, Sarah E. Moran, Rhys Collins, Siddharth Gandhi, Seti Norris, William O. Balmer, Peter Gao, Brayden Roberts, Mark S. Marley, Hannah R. Wakeford, David K. Sing

**Abstract:** The precision of brown dwarf spectra from JWST enables unprecedented insight into the atmospheric and cloud properties of sub-stellar atmospheres. Here, we compare both self-consistent radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) and retrieval atmosphere models to high-SNR 1--18~$\mu$m spectra of two field L-dwarfs from JWST, J0624 (L5) and J2148 (L6--L6.5). Our observations include spectral features from H$_2$O, CO, CO$_2$, CH$_4$, Na, and K and cover approximately 98\% of the outgoing thermal emission from the two objects. We first compare the data to three independent grids of 1D-RCE models: BT-Settl, exoREM, and Sonora Diamondback. While exoREM provides the best fit of the grid models, no 1D-RCE model provides a satisfactory fit to the data, highlighting the complexity of fitting cloudy L-dwarf spectra. Nonetheless, the temperature and cloud properties can be constrained with the 1D-RCE models, while metallicity, C/O ratio, and surface gravity are not well-measured. Next, we use petitRADTRANS to retrieve atmosphere and cloud properties, finding strong evidence for the presence of SiO$_2$ clouds in both objects. The SiO$_2$ is found to be amorphous in structure for J0624 but crystalline in J2148, highlighting important differences in objects of similar spectral type. We also used a non-Bayesian optimization framework to explore a wider variety of cloud scenarios, finding evidence for the inclusion of iron-rich magnesium silicates (Mg$_{0.5}$Fe$_{0.5}$SiO$_3$, MgFeSiO$_4$) in addition to SiO$_2$ in both objects. These results show both the complexity and diversity of brown dwarf cloud properties, while also highlighting the constraining power of broad-wavelength JWST observations of cloudy L-dwarfs.

## 67. [The ultraviolet continuum slopes of galaxies at $\mathbf{z \gtrsim 12}$ selected from ${\mathbf{0.6 \, deg}^2}$ of JWST imaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17208) <a id="link67"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17208

**Authors:** C. Bondestam, D. J. McLeod, F. Cullen, R. J. McLure, J. S. Dunlop, S. Antonogiannaki, H. -H. Leung, R. Begley, A. C. Carnall, C. T. Donnan, R. S. Ellis, A. Fontana, N. A. Grogin, I. J. B. Holst, G. D. Illingworth, A. M. Koekemoer, F. -Y. Liu, T. M. Stanton, S. D. Stevenson, E. Taylor

**Abstract:** We present an analysis of the ultraviolet (UV) continuum slopes $(\beta)$ of $55$ galaxies at $z\gtrsim 12$, selected from a wide-area ($>0.6$ sq. deg) search across publicly available JWST/NIRCam imaging. Our sample spans the absolute UV magnitude ($M_{\mathrm{UV}}$) range $-21.6 \leq M_{\mathrm{UV}} \leq -17.3$ and we find an inverse variance-weighted mean $\langle\beta\rangle = -2.57\pm0.04$ indicating that, on average, the galaxy population is extremely blue at $z\gtrsim 12$. The average $\beta$ at these redshifts is consistent with the intrinsic stellar plus nebular continuum limit in the absence of UV dust-attenuation. Consistent with earlier JWST works, our analysis suggests that the moderately dust-attenuated galaxies at $z \lesssim 10$ become essentially attenuation-free by $z \simeq 11$. We find no evidence for a $\beta-M_{\mathrm{UV}}$ relation in our $z\gtrsim 12$ sample, indicating that the attenuation-free interpretation applies across all observed UV magnitudes. By augmenting our sample with previous JWST constraints down to $z=9$, and incorporating $M_{\mathrm{UV}}$-matched HST studies down to $z=4$, we find a smooth evolution in $\beta(z)$ over a wide range in redshift. The average value of $\beta$ becomes progressively bluer at $z>4$, with $\mathrm{d}\beta/\mathrm{d}z \simeq -0.1$. Finally, although we find that the typical galaxy at $z \gtrsim 12$ is consistent with the attenuation-free limit, the scatter in our individual $\beta$ measurements is consistent with the existence of a small population of dust-reddened galaxies with $\beta \gtrsim -2$.

## 68. [Tracing Galactic Dust Reddening with Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Emission: SPHEREx Observations of the North Ecliptic Pole](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14640) <a id="link68"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14640

**Authors:** Dennis Lee (Gemma), Brandon Hensley (Gemma), Tzu-Ching Chang (Gemma), Olivier Doré (Gemma), Matt Ashby (Gemma), Shuang-Shuang Chen (Gemma), Yun-Ting Cheng (Gemma), Yi-Kuan Chiang (Gemma), Brendan Crill (Gemma), Ari Cukierman (Gemma), Andreas Faisst (Gemma), Joe Hora (Gemma), Zhaoyu (Gemma), Huai, Howard Hui, Woong-Seob Jeong, Miju Kang, Carey Lisse, Dan Masters, Gary Melnick, Chi Nguyen, Roberta Paladini, Ji Yeon Seok, Volker Tolls, Michael Werner, Mike Zemcov

**Abstract:** We investigate the ability of SPHEREx observations of the $3.3$ $\mu$m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission feature to trace Galactic dust reddening. Applying a spectral template-based method to SPHEREx data, we measure the strength of the $3.3$ $\mu$m PAH feature in each $6''.2$ pixel of a $22^{\circ}$ by $22^{\circ}$ region centered on the north ecliptic pole (NEP). We convert the PAH feature strength to reddening by applying a radiation field correction and a linear scale factor. The resulting $E(B-V)$ map is consistent with far-infrared, stellar, and HI-based reddening maps at arcminute scales, exhibiting a typical $E(B-V)$ difference of $\lesssim 7$ mmag. A galaxy count test finds that all reddening maps have a dispersion of $\approx11$ mmag in $E(B-V)$ relative to what would be needed to produce spatially uniform galaxy counts. While there is some evidence that reddening is overestimated by our map at high PAH abundances, this effect is smaller than the uncertainties on the applied radiation field corrections and limited to $\sim$10 mmag in the most extreme regions of the NEP. For a diffuse, high Galactic latitude region like the NEP and at the sensitivities of our validation metrics, the SPHEREx PAH-emission based reddening map matches the accuracy of existing reddening maps while being capable of accessing a higher angular resolution of $\sim6''$.

Scott (Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1, Canada)

**Abstract:** The Euclid space mission is dedicated to probing the nature of dark energy and dark matter, through a comprehensive mapping of the Universe's large-scale structure. Central to these cosmological goals are the spectra produced by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) and reduced by the scientific pipelines of the SIR (Spectral near InfraRed) processing function. Due to the intrinsic complexity of slitless spectroscopic data, scientific observations cannot be self-calibrated by the science pipelines. Consequently, the development of dedicated SIR calibration pipelines, utilising specific pointing sequences and observation fields, is essential. The resulting calibration products are fundamental to ensuring that reduced spectra are characterised within requirements in both wavelength and flux. This paper provides a detailed description of the SIR calibration pipelines responsible for generating the products utilised by the science pipelines for Data Release 1 (DR1). A significant challenge in these calibration tasks arises from the requirement to model the entire focal plane as a unified entity. Such a global modelling approach is critical for maintaining astrometric and spectroscopic continuity across the entire field of view. DR1 provides more than 170 millions validated spectra in both red- and blue-grism modes. The accuracy of the reduced spectra is strictly dependent on the performance of the calibration pipelines. Comprehensive analyses of the calibration products and the resulting science spectra demonstrate that current outputs successfully meet the mission requirements. Nevertheless, specific areas for optimisation have been identified; ongoing development is focused on addressing these critical points to further enhance data quality for future data releases.

## 70. [Influence of Alfven wave turbulence dissipation in stellar winds of the Sun and M dwarfs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14884) <a id="link70"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14884

**Authors:** Kaito Suzuki, Takaaki Yokoyama, Munehito Shoda

**Abstract:** The physics of M-dwarf stellar winds is increasingly being investigated within the framework of wave-driven models. In the case of the solar wind, Alfven-wave turbulence (AWT) is believed to play a crucial role in heating and accelerating the plasma. In this study, we perform one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the solar and M-dwarf winds using a model that incorporates shock heating generated by mode conversion and treats AWT as an optional component. For the solar wind, we confirm that including AWT reproduces the observed predominance of outwardly propagating Alfven waves, supporting the role of turbulent dissipation in driving the wind. We further validate this AWT-driven solar wind directly against Parker Solar Probe observations, finding good agreement in both the location of the Alfven point and the level of the normalized cross helicity in the fast solar wind. In M-dwarf simulations, we find that AWT dominates the overall heating budget within the investigated parameter range. A parameter survey of coronal magnetic field strength reveals that the dependence of the mass-loss rate on Bcor differs qualitatively between cases with and without AWT, highlighting the importance of chromospheric dissipation. In the absence of AWT, the resulting mass-loss rates are broadly consistent with previous studies and observations. In contrast, when AWT is included, the mass-loss rate is significantly reduced because turbulent dissipation decreases the Alfven-wave (Poynting) flux entering the corona. These results suggest that the effects of chromospheric turbulence play a crucial role in modeling M-dwarf winds.

## 71. [Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15879) <a id="link71"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15879

**Authors:** Alisa Galishnikova, Siddhartha Gupta, Anatoly Spitkovsky, Xiaochen Sun

**Abstract:** Shock waves in supernova remnants are thought to accelerate cosmic rays (CRs) via diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). If acceleration is efficient, CR-modified shock models and nonlinear DSA predict smoothly decelerated precursors and concave spectra that harden with energy. These predictions are in tension with observations, which favor spectra closer to the test-particle form, $4 \pi f(p) p^{4} = {\rm const}$ or steeper. We use one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations to follow the long-term nonlinear coupling of the thermal plasma and CR electrons in non-relativistic quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks. We choose electrons over ions for their larger charge per unit mass, probing the limits of current-driven feedback. We vary the supplied CR-electron mass fraction to measure the shock's response. Our injection model determines the effective injection and acceleration from particle trajectories through the evolving upstream turbulence, rather than a prescribed shock injection fraction. The reflected CR-electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing the formation of a spatially extended CR-pressure precursor. Across the CR-electron mass supply explored, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream CR current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle DSA shape across the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure. These results suggest that, once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state largely insensitive to the details of CR injection.

## 72. [Cosmic Ray Heating of the Early IGM: Realistic Galaxy Populations, Reduced Efficiency, and 21-cm Signatures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15858) <a id="link72"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15858

**Authors:** Michael Pagano, Andrei Mesinger, Carmelo Evoli, Sruthi Ravikularaman

**Abstract:** Cosmic rays (CRs) accelerated by the first supernovae could heat the intergalactic medium (IGM) before reionization. Previous 21-cm simulations, assuming a kinetic-energy power-law spectrum and simplified galaxy populations, found that CR heating can rival X-ray heating from high-mass X-ray binaries, imprint a distinct signature on the 21-cm power spectrum, and flatten the absorption trough of the global 21-cm signal. Here we model CR heating in 21cmFAST with: (i) the momentum power-law spectrum predicted by diffusive shock acceleration; (ii) Coulomb losses off free electrons; and (iii) injection from data-informed populations of atomic-cooling and molecularly cooled galaxies. We find that CR heating is about an order of magnitude weaker than previously estimated because a momentum power law places little energy in the sub-relativistic protons ($\lesssim 40$ MeV) that supply 99% of the heat. For our fiducial spectral slope, at the hard end of those inferred for Galactic supernova remnants, and for matched efficiency, this reduces the heating by a factor of $\approx 12$, and together with a more realistic galaxy model, by a factor of $\approx 28$ at $z = 15$. At the efficiencies that supernovae can supply, CR heating is weaker than standard X-ray heating, and the global signal alone cannot tell the two apart. Distinguishing CR from X-ray heating with the 21-cm power spectrum requires CR efficiencies a few times higher than those expected from local observations. At such efficiencies, CR heating yields up to $\approx 55\%$ more power than X-ray heating at matched global signal (median over scales), compared with only 3-6% at a locally motivated efficiency. A flattened absorption trough, like the one claimed by EDGES, requires efficiencies over two orders of magnitude above the local ones, beyond plausible Population III supernova budgets.

## 73. [Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: I. Population Synthesis Framework and Illustrative Examples](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14649) <a id="link73"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14649

**Authors:** Cordelia Dashwood Brown, Poshak Gandhi, Christian Knigge, Yue Zhao, Phil Charles, Pornisara Nuchvanichakul, Katelyn Breivik, Akarsh Sahay, Siddharth Malu

**Abstract:** The natal kicks imparted to neutron stars and black holes at birth are critical for understanding massive-star evolution, compact-object formation, and compact binary merger rates. However, constraining these kicks is challenging, since they cannot be directly observed. Here, we outline a framework for inferring natal kick probability distributions for compact binaries. Our method embeds the rapid binary-population code COSMIC in a Monte-Carlo workflow that evolves ensembles of simulated binaries. From those which host compact objects, we can select subsets that match the observational characteristics of any given system (e.g. component masses, orbital period, mass-transfer status, systemic velocity). As a proof-of-concept, we apply this framework to six compact binaries spanning a wide range of companion masses and compact-object types. For each system, we identify the evolutionary channel(s) that could have led to the current observational characteristics, and isolate regions of allowed natal kicks and progenitor parameter space. We reconfirm that at least one black hole system, XTE J1118+480, must have received a natal kick $v_{\rm NK} > 100$ km s$^{-1}$. The neutron-star system, GX 301-2, is also inferred to have received an impulsive kick exceeding 280 km s$^{-1}$. We discuss the strengths and limitations associated with population-synthesis-based inference methods and explore the effects of adopting different prescriptions for critical binary evolution phases. We provide a detailed demonstration of the non-linear relationship between $v_{\rm NK}$ and $v_{\rm sys}$, highlighting the shortcomings of relying on observations alone to measure natal kicks. The inferred kick velocity distributions across our benchmark sample are generally consistent with previous constraints.

## 74. [The ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR): Initial Data Release (DR1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16166) <a id="link74"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16166

**Authors:** Matthew J. Graham, Samuel Whitebook, Andrew J. Drake, Thomas Prince, Thomas Culino, Ilaria Caiazzo, Jan van Roestel, Zach Vanderbosch, Theo du Laz, Przemek Mroz, Kevin Burdge

**Abstract:** The Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) has observed the northern sky observable from Palomar Observatory since March 2018, accumulating a median of a thousand photometric measurements across $gri$ for each of more than a billion sources. Among these billions of objects are millions of periodically variable stars, active galactic nuclei, stellar remnants, and substellar objects. We describe the initial data release (DR1) of the ZTF Variability Archive (ZVAR) which provides image difference forced photometry, candidate periods, and variability metrics for approximately 1.3 billion sources in ZTF having an identification in Pan-STARRS1 DR1 (PS1). The data cover the 5.37 year interval between March 2018 and July 2023. ZVAR is sensitive to periods between 5 minutes and 2.7 years. We also describe tools for accessing the ZVAR data.

## 75. [Can we constrain cosmology with compound gravitational lenses?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15714) <a id="link75"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15714

**Authors:** Duncan J. Bowden, Tian Li, Aprajita Verma, Thomas E. Collett, Philip Holloway

**Abstract:** Compound lensing in double-source-plane lenses (DSPLs) introduces multiple mass-sheet transformations that bias the inferred distance ratios $\beta$ used to constrain cosmology. We present the recovered $\beta$ from lens models of simulated compound lenses and explore the systematic biases that arise from a mass-sheet transformation in the first source plane. We examined simulated observations based on SDSS J0946+1006, in which we varied the matter distribution of source 1. We found a strong correlation between the stellar-to-halo mass and the recovered $\beta$. We produced a simulated catalogue of DSPLs detectable by the Euclid telescope to see if the same systematic propagates to a more varied population. But at Euclid's resolution, the properties of source 1 were poorly constrained, and any correlated bias was lost in the statistical uncertainty. We inferred $w_0$ and $\Omega_{\rm m}$ for a flat $w$CDM cosmology from our $\beta$ posteriors for our combined sample. We found the cosmology biased when using the full mock Euclid sample, but reduced the bias substantially using a limited, well-modelled ''gold'' sub-sample, bringing it to within $\sim2\sigma$ and $\sim1\sigma$ of the ground-truth cosmology for simulated Euclid and Hubble Space Telescope imaging, respectively. Therefore, we must eliminate systems with unreliable lensing information, and for extreme compound lensing, the model complexity must be sufficient to reproduce the lensing observations. DSPLs remain a promising cosmological probe that could provide independent and complementary constraints to existing probes.

## 76. [Parallel alignment of radio AGN jets and large cosmic web structures in the direction of the Shapley supercluster](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17202) <a id="link76"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17202

**Authors:** I. Baronchelli, T. Venturi, V. Casasola, P. Merluzzi, C. Burigana, G. Busarello, M. Bonato, O. Smirnov, T. Ronconi, M. Massardi, E. Liuzzo

**Abstract:** Aims. We investigated the potential large-scale alignment of radio active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets in the proximity of the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) area and its correlation with the identified cosmic web structures. Methods. We analyzed 28 radio AGNs divided into two populations with comparable sky coverage north and south of a diffuse X-ray filamentary structure connecting clusters in the SSC core. We measured the average jet position angles (PAs) and combined them with spectroscopic redshifts to assess the persistence of the alignment along the line of sight. Results. We detected a significant large-scale alignment of the radio AGN jets with the foreground X-ray filament (oriented at PA $\sim$ 115$^\circ$ $\pm$ 10$^\circ$). Both the northern (PA $\sim$ 117$^\circ$) and southern (PA $\sim$ 129$^\circ$) groups align with this axis, yielding an overall statistical significance of 4.5 $\sigma$ (upper and lower bounds: 6.1$\sigma$, 3.8 $\sigma$). Although the projected alignment is highly significant, sparse spectroscopic coverage (seven sources spanning 0.048 $\lesssim$ z $\lesssim$ 0.55) suggests that this spatial coherence may extend beyond the SSC (z $\sim$ 0.048), hinting at a line-of-sight correlation across significantly larger cosmic scales. Conclusions. The observed alignment cannot be explained by localized dynamical processes alone. These findings may indicate a persistent influence of the large-scale structure of the cosmic web, or preferred directions of matter collapse, on supermassive black hole spin axes, highlighting a connection between AGN jet morphology and the underlying dark matter distribution. Such alignments represent an important systematic that must be accounted for in precision cosmology with surveys such as Euclid.

## 77. [$r$-Largest Order Statistics for Galaxy Cluster Cosmology I: Reconstruction of the high-mass end of the Halo Mass Function](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15398) <a id="link77"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15398

**Authors:** T. Gayoux, P-S. Corasaniti

**Abstract:** We introduce the $r$-largest order statistics ($r$-LOS) framework for galaxy clusters, a generalization of the standard extreme value statistics (EVS) approach. While conventional EVS focuses on the probability distribution of the most massive cluster within a given volume, the $r$-LOS framework exploits the additional statistical information encoded in the joint distribution of the $r$ most massive clusters, ranked in descending order of mass. We develop the corresponding mathematical formalism, discuss its asymptotic properties, and derive a set of relations relevant to galaxy cluster cosmology. In particular, we demonstrate that the high-mass end of the halo mass function (HMF) can be reconstructed from the generalized extreme value (GEV) parameters inferred using an extension of the block maxima method that incorporates the $r$ most massive clusters in each volume. This provides a means of recovering the high-mass tail of the HMF using only a small subsample of the halo population. We validate these relations using both comoving and light-cone halo catalogues from numerical simulations. Finally, we investigate the sensitivity of the $r$-LOS framework to primordial non-Gaussianity, focusing on its impact on the statistics of massive clusters.

## 78. [Non-Gaussian matter fluctuations from primordial magnetic fields and galaxy luminosity function](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15188) <a id="link78"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15188

**Authors:** Teppei Minoda, Yi Mao, Shohei Saga, Hayato Shimabukuro

**Abstract:** Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) represent a promising candidate for the origin of large-scale magnetic fields observed in astrophysical environments. Through the Lorentz force, PMFs generate matter density perturbations, leaving distinct imprints on the formation of cosmic structures. While previous studies have primarily characterized these imprints via the matter power spectrum --- a two-point statistic --- we demonstrate that the one-point statistics of PMF-induced density fluctuations reveal an intrinsically non-Gaussian probability distribution function (PDF), even when the PMFs themselves are statistically Gaussian. In particular, we find that the high-density tail of the PDF is enhanced by over two orders of magnitude relative to the Gaussian case. Adopting the Press-Schechter formalism, we show that this non-Gaussianity significantly boosts the abundance of rare objects, especially massive halos and those at high redshifts. We further compute the ultraviolet luminosity function of galaxies at $z=6$, $12$, and $16$, and compare our predictions with recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations that have reported an excess of high-redshift galaxies at $z\sim 12$ -- $16$ relative to standard $\Lambda$CDM expectations. Intriguingly, in the limiting case where the total density field inherits this PDF, our results suggest that the non-Gaussian density fluctuations sourced by PMFs can explain the bright-end ($M_\mathrm{UV}\lesssim -18$) excess at $z\gtrsim 12$, without requiring additional astrophysical enhancements to star-formation efficiency.

**Abstract:** The Euclid mission is revolutionising the study of strong gravitational lenses by providing high-resolution imaging over an unprecedented survey area, increasing the number of known lenses by two orders of magnitude compared to previous surveys. Characterising this sample of lens-galaxies requires accurate measurements of their physical properties. However, standard catalogue photometry often blends the light from the foreground lens and the lensed background source, limiting the reliability of derived galaxy parameters. We present a homogeneous catalogue of photometric redshifts and physical properties for 9538 galaxy-scale strong lenses identified in Euclid's DR1 strong-lens sample. We use deblended multiwavelength photometry obtained from the lens modelling of Euclid and ground-based images with PyAutoLens. The photometric redshifts of the lens galaxies are estimated using the template-fitting code Phosphoros. The stellar masses, SFRs, stellar ages, and metallicities are inferred through SED fitting with Prospector, adopting a flexible non-parametric SFH and a Salpeter IMF. The robustness of the inferred parameters is assessed through comparisons with spectroscopic redshifts and external galaxy surveys. The sample of lenses spans a broad redshift range of $0.13\lesssim z_{\rm phot} \lesssim 1.98$, with a median $z_{\rm phot} = 0.68^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$. The sample is dominated by massive quiescent galaxies with a $M_\ast$ range $[10^{10},\,10^{12.1}]\,M_\odot$ and a median $\log_{10}(M_\ast/M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$. This catalogue represents one of the first large-scale characterisations of strong-lens galaxies in the Euclid era. By combining deblended photometry with homogeneous photometric redshift and SED-fitting analyses, it provides a foundation for studies of galaxy evolution, lens-galaxy scaling relations, and the connection between stellar and total mass in strong lenses.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 5

## 80. [Variations in the Extinction Curve at High Galactic Latitudes as seen by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14639) <a id="link80"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14639

**Authors:** Sarv Parteek Singh, Edward F. Schlafly, Rongpu Zhou, Sergey E. Koposov, Joan R. Najita, J. Aguilar, S. Ahlen, C. Allende Prieto, D. Bianchi, D. Brooks, A. Carnero Rosell, F. J. Castander, E. Chaussidon, T. Claybaugh, A. P. Cooper, A. Cuceu, K. S. Dawson, A. de la Macorra, Biprateep Dey, P. Doel, S. Ferraro, J. E. Forero-Romero, E. Gaztañaga, Satya Gontcho A Gontcho, G. Gutierrez, J. Guy, C. Hahn, H. K. Herrera-Alcantar, R. Joyce, T. Karim, R. Kehoe, D. Kirkby, A. Kremin, A. Lambert, C. Lamman, M. Landriau, L. Le Guillou, M. E. Levi, M. Manera, P. Martini, A. Meisner, R. Miquel, J. Moustakas, A. D. Myers, S. Nadathur, J. A. Newman, E. Paillas, W. J. Percival, C. Poppett, F. Prada, I. Pérez-Ràfols, C. Ravoux, G. Rossi, R. Ruggeri, L. Samushia, E. Sanchez, C. Saulder, D. Schlegel, M. Schubnell, H. Seo, J. Silber, M. Siudek, G. Tarlé, B. A. Weaver, H. Zou

**Abstract:** The dust extinction curve, characterized by the total-to-selective extinction ratio, $R(V)$, varies with grain size and composition. Accurate $R(V)$ values are crucial for dereddening astronomical colors and understanding the interstellar medium. We measure extinction toward stars with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy using a machine-learning-based relative of the "pair method," matching reddened and unreddened stars. We use XGBoost to predict stars' intrinsic colors from their spectroscopic parameters ($T_\mathrm{eff}$, $\log g$, $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$) and subtract them from observed colors to measure reddening in combinations of the $g$, $r$, $z$, $W1$, and $W2$ bands. This approach directly measures reddening, unlike the common thermal-emission-based method of Schlegel et al. (1998; SFD). The reddening is accurate to roughly 0.02 mag in $g-r$ and $r-z$. We develop a forward model to map $g-r$ and $g-W1$ reddenings to $R(V)$ and find significant variation in $R(V)$, with $\sigma_\mathrm{NMAD}(R(V)) = 0.23$, in dusty regions ($E(g-r) > 0.1$) at high Galactic latitudes observed by DESI. In this footprint, $R(V)$ is bimodal, with modes at 2.9 and 3.4, likely due to large-spatial-scale correlations in the shape of the extinction curve combined with the relatively small number of distinct sightlines with substantial reddening. We find no strong relationship between $R(V)$ and other tracers of the interstellar medium, such as thermal emission, dust temperature, spectral emissivity index $\beta$, and $H\alpha$. However, the error in the SFD-predicted extinction correlates well with $R(V)$, implying that a single optical reddening combined with the far-infrared dust brightness can predict variations in the extinction curve.

**Novelty:** 5

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17242

**Authors:** A. Eranhalodi, J. Nordin, M. Kowalski, U. Burgaz, F. Fischer, M. Ginolin, Y. -L. Kim, T. E. Müller-Bravo, J. Sollerman, A. Townsend, A. Drake, M. Graham, D. Hale, J. C. Jaimes, R. R. Laher, J. Purdum

**Abstract:** Galaxy cluster cores, characterised by old stellar population and suppressed star-formation are ideal for studying the environmental dependence of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). It is unclear whether the diversity of SNe Ia, parametrised by light curve stretch, stems from distinct explosion mechanisms or varying initial conditions, both closely tied to progenitor age. We analyse the light curve stretch and colour distribution of photometrically identified SNe Ia within the galaxy clusters cores, utilising the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) archival data. Using the AMPEL platform, we filter 89,025 ZTF transients spatially coincident with our galaxy cluster catalogues to identify 4,969 likely SN Ia candidates. We split this sample into three populations: core cluster SNe Ia $r \le 0.5R_{500}$, outer-core cluster SNe Ia $0.5R_{500}< r\le 2R_{500}$, and a reference population of non-cluster SN Ia. We present the largest sample of photometrically identified cluster SNe Ia to date, notably isolating a population of 242 SNe Ia within innermost cluster cores $r \le 0.5R_{500}$. This fast-declining SN Ia population is statistically different from the outer-core cluster and field SN Ia population at $\sim4\sigma$ level. A marginal statistical preference for a bimodal distribution over a unimodal one $\Delta AIC$ of 1.53 and 2.3 for each catalogue, indicate cluster cores almost entirely host fast-declining SNe Ia. Conversely, the colour distribution show no significant environmental variation. By filtering out the prompt SN Ia population, cluster cores provide an environment to directly probe the delayed SN Ia progenitor channel. Our observations support a two-population model where progenitor age drives the light curve stretch diversity. The low-stretch values observed in core cluster SNe Ia suggest sub-Chandrasekhar mass double degenerate systems as their likely progenitors.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 5

## 82. [What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15385) <a id="link82"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15385

**Authors:** V. P. Utrobin (NRC "Kurchatov Institute", Moscow, Russia, Institute of Astronomy, Moscow, Russia), N. N. Chugai (Institute of Astronomy, Moscow, Russia)

**Abstract:** We explore the origin of an initial broad luminosity peak that precedes the light curve plateau in type IIP supernovae. It is well known that the explosion of an evolutionary red supergiant model in the frame of radiation hydrodynamics fails to reproduce the initial luminosity peak. A common practice to compensate this drawback is to introduce massive (> 0.3 Msun) circumstellar shell attached to the evolutionary model. This remedy, however, has a negative side effect - a strong deceleration of the outer ejecta, which is inconsistent with early spectral data. An alternative way out suggests modification of a hydrogen envelope of the evolutionary red supergiant model - the outer layers should have steeper density gradient. We perform the search for the optimal multi-parameter hydrodynamic model of type IIP SN 1999em based on the Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. The major result is that the initial luminous peak is well reproduced by the explosion of the red supergiant with the logarithmic density gradient smaller than -3 in the outer layers of about 0.9 Msun. We suggest that the mechanism for the density steepening in the hydrogen envelope is closely related to the unknown mechanism responsible for the creation of the ubiquitous low-mass (< 0.01 Msun) dense confined shell detected in type IIP supernovae.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 5

**Abstract:** This paper describes the characteristics of the Euclid visible imager (VIS) data delivered as part of the Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). This data set contains 42092 calibrated frames. Validated nominal exposures cover 2092 deg$^2$ of sky. We outline the minor changes made to the VIS processing function (PF) since previous releases. For the wide survey, the photometric and astrometric accuracy of the reference stellar sample $(18.5 < I_{\rm E} < 19.8)$ is excellent. The internal and external astrometric dispersions are 0.08 and 0.18 mas, respectively, at the quadrant level, and 3.4 and 5.6 mas at the source level. The corresponding internal and external photometric dispersions are 0.76 and 1.4 mmag at the quadrant level, and 11 and 25 mmag at the source level. We characterise remaining astrometric and photometric systematic effects: focal-plane-dependent variations; time-dependent photometric offsets; and colour-dependent centroid shifts. The noise floor in the deepest VIS images appears to be set by the extended diffuse light of faint galaxies. Globally, the DR1 VIS data meet pre-launch mission requirements and the 42092 images it contains provide our first substantial look at the sky as seen by VIS.

## 84. [The 21 cm-Lyman-$\alpha$ forest cross-power spectrum with a minimal effective field theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17177) <a id="link84"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17177

**Authors:** G. Autieri, V. Iršič, M. Viel

**Abstract:** Intensity maps of the 21 cm line and the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly$\alpha$) forest trace the same cosmic volume at $2\lesssim z\lesssim 4$. Their cross-power spectrum is insensitive to foregrounds that do not correlate between the two probes and, together with the Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectrum, separates the mean 21 cm brightness temperature from the neutral hydrogen (HI) bias. Effective field theory models of each tracer exist, but at one loop they carry tens of nuisance parameters. We test whether a minimal effective field theory (mEFT), consisting of the tree-level Kaiser model with leading-order counterterms and stochastic terms, previously validated for the Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectrum, describes the 21 cm auto-, Ly$\alpha$ auto- and cross-power spectra jointly. We use the Sherwood 80 $h^{-1}$Mpc hydrodynamical simulation with HI painted onto halos at $z=2.4$-$4.2$, and reduce sample variance with Zel'dovich control variates. Each spectrum is validated separately and then in a joint fit with shared parameters. With scale cuts $k_{\rm max}=0.5$, $1.2$ and $2.0\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ for the 21 cm auto-, cross- and Ly$\alpha$ auto-spectra, the mEFT fits all three spectra at all five redshifts. In the joint fit the mEFT determines the HI bias to 2.0-2.5% and the Ly$\alpha$ density bias to 2.1-2.3%. The scale cuts follow the HI velocity dispersion and the Ly$\alpha$ pressure-smoothing scale. When the brightness temperature is left free, the fits that include the cross-spectrum prefer values 20-30% above the true one, at 1-2$\sigma$, while the two auto-spectra together do not constrain it. A prior on the HI bias recovers the true value of the brightness temperature.

## 85. [Dissecting and diagnosing the LISA Galactic binary population](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16611) <a id="link85"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16611

**Authors:** Alice E. Cravioglio, Arianna I. Renzini

**Abstract:** LISA will individually resolve thousands of Galactic double white dwarf (DWD) binaries, while the majority stays buried in an unresolved gravitational wave (GW) confusion foreground. Which systems get resolved depends on the binary's parameters, on the global population and on instrumental sensitivity, so the resolved population is not a representative sample of the underlying Galactic population. Interpreting LISA's future catalog therefore requires understanding these selection effects. Here we characterize the resolved and unresolved subpopulations of a simulated Milky Way DWD catalog, using an iterative subtraction pipeline applied over different observation times. Resolvability is driven primarily by chirp mass: higher chirp mass, inspiraling systems are strongly favored over lower mass, outspiraling or monochromatic ones, and this reflects on the rate with which different composition subtypes are resolved. Spatially, resolved sources trace the Galactic bulge, because it is intrinsically the densest region of the Galaxy. The confusion background shows an internal bimodal chirp-mass structure, and is not generated uniformly by the same subpopulation in different frequency bands. We introduce a diagnostic for the minimum number of sources needed to reproduce a given fraction of the confusion power in a frequency band, and show that a residual confusion floor persists even after 100 years of integration. These biases are significant and need to be accounted for when using LISA's resolved DWD catalog and the confusion background to constrain the Galactic DWD population.

## 86. [An analytic diffusion model for viewing-angle effects in explosive transients](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15905) <a id="link86"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15905

**Authors:** Daniella van der Boom, Doron Kushnir

**Abstract:** The tight observed relation between the peak bolometric luminosity, $L_{\mathrm p}$, and the width ratio $L_{30}/L_{\mathrm p}$ of Type Ia supernovae, with $L_{30}$ the luminosity 30 d after explosion, makes viewing-angle effects a useful test of explosion models. We develop an analytic diffusion model for homologously expanding asymmetric ejecta with uniform density and grey opacity, based on a Green's-function solution and an Eddington surface-emission prescription, and obtain angle-dependent light curves for a displaced spherical source and for oblate ejecta. We validate them against Monte Carlo (MC) radiative transfer and derive geometric approximations to the peak-luminosity anisotropy. For a displaced spherical source, the quasi-steady approximation, equivalent to stationary diffusion in frozen ejecta, gives $L_{\mathrm p}(\theta)/L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}\simeq1+(17/8)z_{\mathrm{off}}\cos\theta$, where $z_{\mathrm{off}}$ is the displacement in units of the ejecta radius, $\theta$ the viewing angle from the displacement axis, and $L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}$ the angle-averaged peak. This dipole is $\mathord{\approx}10$ per cent below the finite-time value in the tested configurations. For oblate ejecta, the leading term is quadrupolar and is set by a single shape parameter. Effective models of 19 off-centre sub-Chandrasekhar explosions recover the MC peak times, peak luminosities, and width ratios to median errors of 3, 4, and 6 per cent, and the extent in $L_{\mathrm p}$ of the MC tracks, but underestimate the width-ratio variation with viewing angle by a factor of 2 to 3. An oblate construction captures the scale of peak luminosity variations in six equal-mass white-dwarf collisions. The model tracks remain inconsistent with the observed distribution, and for asymmetric models the transverse viewing-angle variation adds to the tension.

## 87. [Euclid First Data Release 1 (DR1) - Data release overview](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16510) <a id="link87"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16510

**Authors:** Euclid Collaboration, Herve Aussel

**Abstract:** This paper describes the contents of the Euclid First Data Release (DR1), together with the set of papers that document the data-processing and the data products. DR1 consists of two parts: first `DR1-Foundation', releasing images, spectra, and catalogues in November 2026. Second, the shear measurements and the `Level~3' products required for cosmological analyses will be added in June 2027 to complete the full DR1. ## 88. [The Gaia-alerted 2024--2025 brightening of V346 Nor](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14723) <a id="link88"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14723

**Authors:** Á. Kóspál, D. J. Lengyel, P. Ábrahám, B. M. Marosi, F. Cruz-Sáenz de Miera, E. Fiorellino, T. Giannini, S. Kraus, A. Labdon, P. W. Lucas, Th. Moore, Zs. Nagy, M. Siwak, A. Udalski

**Abstract:** Young stellar objects (YSOs) build their final mass through a highly unsteady, episodic accretion process, often accompanied by outflow and ejection events. Objects undergoing episodic high-accretion states are known as eruptive YSOs. V346 Nor is an embedded eruptive YSO that underwent a sudden optical brightening in 2024 July that triggered an alert from the Gaia Photometric Science Alert system. With the aim of characterizing the physical processes behind this recent brightening event, we analyze new and archival photometric and spectroscopic monitoring data. We study how the brightness, colors, and spectral features changed with time in the past decade. We also fitted an accretion disk model to the observations in which the stellar mass--accretion rate product $M_{\star}\dot{M}$ and the line-of-sight extinction $A_V$ are free parameters. The accretion rate in V346 Nor has been higher ($M_{\star}\dot{M} \sim 10^{-4}\,M_{\odot}^2\,$yr$^{-1}$) since 2021 than during any previous historical peak, although it was relatively constant during the 2025 February-May brightness maximum, which was driven instead by a drop in extinction from $A_V \approx 20$\,mag to $10$\,mag. V346 Nor has accreted about 2\% of the stellar mass since its outburst. A P Cygni profile in H$\alpha$ indicates a strong outflowing wind reminiscent of classical FUors. The variability of the CaII infrared triplet lines and transient CO bandhead emission point to a highly unstable inner disk and accretion region. The persistence of forbidden line emission indicates ongoing jet activity. The brightness and color variations of V346 Nor are the result of a superposition of changes in the accretion rate and the line-of-sight extinction. With record-high accretion levels and strong wind and jet activity, V346 Nor is in one of its most active phases since its original outburst in the 1970s.

## 89. [Enhanced Early Structure from Axiodilatons & 21cm Observations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15647) <a id="link89"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15647

**Authors:** Chan Youn Weon, Carsten van de Bruck, C. P. Burgess, Jeong Han Kim, Adam Smith

**Abstract:** Axiodilatons provide a promising unified model of the Dark Sector whose properties are motivated by the use of accidental approximate symmetries to embed the light fields needed for observations into well-motivated UV physics in a technically natural way. These models turn out to help ameliorate many current puzzles in $\Lambda$CDM phenomenology (e.g. the Hubble tension and the evidence for evolving Dark Energy) `for free' despite not being designed for that purpose. We here explore in more detail another serendipitous feature of these models: their tendency to enhance early structure formation, in a way that seems suggestive given the accumulating evidence for structure arising earlier than expected in $\Lambda$CDM. Since early structure growth is the cleanest to study we explore in detail the expected 21cm signal produced by axiodilaton models, using the same parameter choices that improve agreement with observations elsewhere in cosmology. For fixed astrophysics, we forecast that SKA1-Low could distinguish dilaton couplings as small as a few times $10^{-2}$ from $\Lambda$CDM at $2\sigma$, mainly because of the earlier formation of structure. ## 92. [A flash before dawn: 21 cm signatures of transient reionization from supermassive Pop III stars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16006) <a id="link92"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16006

**Authors:** Nicholas Kern, Prakhar Bansal, Dragan Huterer

**Abstract:** Recent data from cosmological galaxy surveys combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data give a preference for a departure from $\Lambda$CDM, favoring a model with an evolving dark energy equation of state or a small neutrino mass. We find that the 21 cm power spectrum probed by future radio survey arrays like the Square Kilometre Array could detect signatures of these supermassive population III at high significance and set model-dependent constraints on $\tau$ that approach $\sigma_\tau\sim0.012$, enough to distinguish our fiducial $\tau\sim0.097$ scenario from current Planck values at $>3\sigma$.

Our results highlight how the initially more centrally concentrated P2 drives a steeper radial gradient and a steeper MF slope in the outer regions, which subsequently affects the global cluster values. Motivated by recent observational studies suggesting that a bottom-light IMF may better describe massive globular clusters, as well as measurements of a flatter P2 MF slope in the outer regions of 47 Tucanae, we additionally explore a three-parameter bottom-light IMF and a simulation in which the P1 IMF differs from the P2 IMF, with the P2 IMF flatter than that of the P1 in the lower mass range.

## 101. [Do magnetic cycles of Sun-like stars exhibit Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15956) <a id="link101"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15956

**Authors:** Suyog Garg, Bidya Binay Karak

**Abstract:** One intriguing feature of the solar magnetic cycle is its alternating cycle amplitude: the even-numbered cycles are usually followed by stronger odd-numbered cycles, popularly known as the Gnevyshev-Ohl rule (or the even-odd effect). In this study, we probe whether Gnevyshev-Ohl-like trends exist in stellar cycles of Sun-like stars, utilizing the Mount Wilson Observatory (MWO) chromospheric $S$-index data as a proxy for the stellar magnetic field. We apply quasi-Planck and skewed-Gaussian function fits to extract the cycle peaks from the MWO $S$-index data and consider the stars that have a minimum of four usable cycles. First, we say that Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule is obeyed in any star for a pair of even-odd or odd-even cycles, if the second cycle in the pair is stronger. For this definition, we find that many of the stars considered, especially slow rotators, hold the Gnevyshev-Ohl-like trends quite well, with the fraction of cycles obeying the GO-rule been $1.0$ for these stars. However, we do not find any significant correlation between the fraction of cycles obeying the rule and the rotation period or the Rossby number of the star. Next, we examine Gnevyshev-Ohl-like rule in the stellar cycles using alternative definitions for the rule. Saying that the rule holds as long as the middle cycle has a maximum or minimum in sets of consecutive three cycles, we obtain a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.25 $(p=0.299)$ and 0.59 (0.007), between the GO-rule fraction and the rotation period and Rossby number respectively, for the skewed-Gaussian fit data. Inspite of the fact, that our analysis suffers from a lack of sufficient number of good-quality cycles, we be believe that our results can still shed some light on the dynamo mechanism in other Sun-like stars and its dependence on rotation.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 4

## 102. [What the X-ray Emission from Young Supernovae Can Tell Us About Their Progenitors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16216) <a id="link102"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16216

**Authors:** Vikram Dwarkadas (University of Chicago)

**Abstract:** We discuss constraints that the X-ray emission from supernovae can place on their progenitor stars. Since almost all X-ray supernovae arise from massive stars, we concentrate on implications for massive stars. These stars lose mass throughout their lifetime in the form of stellar winds. X-ray emission can be used to gauge the wind properties, especially the mass-loss rates, via various techniques. The abundance of various elements formed by nucleosynthesis within the stars, and released in the stellar explosion, can be estimated from X-ray spectra. In many cases, a combination of X-ray light curves and spectra can allow us to extricate the structure and morphology of the surrounding medium formed by pre-supernova mass loss into which the SN shock is expanding.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 4

## 103. [MeerKAT and ASKAP EMU new radio-continuum observations of Wolf-Rayet nebula PCG 11 (Cohen's Ring)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16134) <a id="link103"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16134

**Authors:** M. D. Filipović, Z. J. Smeaton, A. C. Bradley, R. Z. E. Alsaberi, H. Sano, L. Barnes, C. Buemi, C. Bordiu, A. Brunetti, F. Bufano, F. Cavallaro, E. J. Crawford, Y. Fukui, A. J. Green, A. M. Hopkins, A. Ingallinera, R. Kothes, S. Lazarević, D. Leahy, S. Loru, K. Luken, M. Mallows, Q. A. Parker, J. L. Payne, G. Rowell, M. Stupar, N. F. H. Tothill, K. Tsuge, G. M. Umana, D. Urošević, S. F. ur Rahman, J. Th. van Loon

**Abstract:** We present new radio-continuum observations of the well-known Wolf-Rayet (WR) nebula PCG 11 (Cohen's Ring; named after and in honour of the co-author on the discovery paper, Martin Cohen) using observations from the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP) Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU), Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) and MeerKAT surveys. We find that the elliptical shell surrounding Cohen's Ring has a flux density of 62$\pm$2\,mJy at 1000 MHz. The angular size of the elliptical emission is measured to be 54\arcsec$\times$45\arcsec\ (at P.A.=69.4\D), which agrees well with observations of the source in H$\alpha$ and at 24\,$\mu$m in the infrared. Using the measured angular size and a distance of 3.94$\pm$0.27\,kpc, we determine that the nebula has a linear size of $1.03(\pm0.07)\times0.86(\pm0.06)$\,pc. Together with our new and previously measured flux density estimates, we determine a spectral index for Cohen's Ring to be $\alpha$=0.06$\pm$0.02, indicating that the emission from the WR nebula is of thermal origin. Based on a typical average expansion velocity of 75~km~s$^{-1}$ for a WR star with a Red Supergiant (RSG) progenitor, we estimate the age of Cohen's Ring to be $\sim$ 13500 years. Our NANTEN telescope CO observations suggest that Cohen's Ring was formed during a relatively recent mass-loss event, while the associated CO-emitting molecular gas reflects the cumulative effects of stellar-wind feedback over a much longer timescale ($\sim$1.5\,Myr). As one of the few WR ring nebulae with linked molecular gas, Cohen's Ring provides a valuable laboratory for studying the long-term impact of massive-star feedback on surrounding molecular clouds.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 4

A. Walton (Institute of Astronomy, University of Cambridge, Madingley Road, Cambridge CB3 0HA, UK), A. H. Wright (Ruhr University Bochum, Faculty of Physics and Astronomy, Astronomical Institute), D. Scott (Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1, Canada)

**Abstract:** The Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) contains catalogues of sources covering 1900 deg2, including deep coverage of legacy fields that enable an extensive comparison between Euclid imaging and multiwavelength observations from other instruments. The Cosmic Evolution Survey (COSMOS) field, observed by Euclid and included in DR1, has been observed with the James Webb Space Telescope, resulting in the COSMOS2025 catalogue. We compare the Euclid DR1 photometry with the multiwavelength COSMOS2025 data to assess the accuracy of the photometric measurements produced by the different methods implemented in the OU-MER pipeline. We use both the Euclid Wide and Deep Surveys, focussing exclusively on extragalactic sources. We use the fluxes of COSMOS2025 to predict the expected fluxes in the Euclid bands via spectral energy distribution fitting, while the redshifts are either spectroscopic, for a sample of brighter sources, or photometric, to include fainter sources. Both the fluxes in the common Hyper Suprime-Cam bands and the SEDs from COSMOS2025 are used to validate the analysis and to characterise any biases or limitations of the method. The predicted fluxes and the OU-MER measurements are in good agreement, especially for bright and isolated sources. Median offsets depend on band, photometric method, survey depth, and redshift sample, most well within 10%, the largest offset seen in the NIR bands for the deep photo-z model-fitting measurements. However, complementary measurements on Gaia stars show an opposite trend, highlighting that photometric validation approaches may suffer from intrinsic uncertainties that prevent a thorough assessment of systematic effects. Among the three methods, template-fitting photometry generally shows the smallest offset from the SED-based predictions in the NISP bands and toward fainter magnitudes, while aperture photometry and model-fitting are comparable in IE.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 4

## 105. [Non-evolutionary effects on period change in Magellanic Cepheids. III. Empirical connection with additional low-amplitude variability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17079) <a id="link105"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.17079

**Authors:** Rajeev Singh Rathour, Rados{ł}aw Smolec, Vincent Hocdé, Nicolas Nardetto, Oliwia Zió{ł}kowska, Igor Soszyński, Andrzej Udalski

**Abstract:** The O-C method in classical Cepheids traces both evolutionary and shorter-timescale (non-evolutionary) period changes. In our previous works, we found irregular period changes in $\sim$33% of Magellanic classical Cepheids, but excluded Cepheids showing additional low-amplitude variability. Here, we establish whether first-overtone Cepheids hosting such variability differ in their period-change behaviour from the general first-overtone population. We analyse 544 Magellanic Cepheids with period ratios $P_{\rm x}/P_{\rm 1O} \sim 0.60-0.65$ or $P_{\rm 1O}/P_{\rm x} \sim 0.68$, using OGLE photometry, and classify and characterise their O-C diagrams following our previous studies. We find irregular period changes in 339 first-overtone Cepheids (195 in the LMC and 144 in the SMC), an incidence rate of $\sim$75.5%, a statistically significant increase over the $\sim$68.1% of our previous single-mode first-overtone sample. The combined first-overtone incidence becomes $\sim$69.7%. This provides the first empirical connection between additional low-amplitude variability and irregular period changes in first-overtone Cepheids. At a fixed pulsation period, the irregularity strength anticorrelates with the dominant pulsation amplitude but not with the additional-signal amplitude, suggesting that the additional periodicity marks a weakly saturated pulsation state rather than driving the irregularity. We further detect cycle-to-cycle (C2C) period variation in 37% of the class 3 sample, with jitter roughly seven times larger than in non-Blazhko RRc stars and a shallower scaling with pulsation period.

**Novelty:** 4

H. Wright (Ruhr University Bochum, Faculty of Physics and Astronomy, Astronomical Institute), H. Boquet (Centre de Calcul de l'IN2P3/CNRS, 21 avenue Pierre de Coubertin 69627 Villeurbanne Cedex, France), D. Scott (Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1, Canada)

**Abstract:** The Euclid mission is designed to address fundamental questions on the nature of dark energy and dark matter by mapping the extragalactic sky with a wide-area survey complemented by targeted deep observations. The required scientific performance places stringent demands on the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), which transforms raw telemetry into calibrated, validated, and scientifically exploitable products. The SGS is a distributed system comprising the Euclid Science Operations Centre, the Science Data Centres, Instrument Operation Teams, and supporting Organisation Units, within a common architectural and procedural framework. This paper presents the SGS as implemented for Data Release 1 (DR1), describing its organisation, architecture, processing functions, and operational model. We outline the main components of the SGS common infrastructure. A key element is the Euclid Archive System (EAS), the central metadata repository based on a common data model. It comprises a Distributed Storage System, providing scalable storage of data files across the Science Data Centres; a Data Processing System used by the pipelines to register and access files and their lineage; and a Science Archive, distributing validated data products. Processing is coordinated by a common orchestration framework based on the Infrastructure Abstraction Layer, providing workflow management and resource abstraction of distributed compute clusters. Software development, integration, and deployment are supported by the Common Development Environment. We describe daily operations, calibration, and quality control, followed by the DR1 production campaign, including processing flows, validation strategy, and computational and data volumes. This infrastructure enabled Euclid DR1, involving 35 million jobs across nine Science Data Centres and 6.7 million core-hours, demonstrating robustness and scalability of the SGS.

**Novelty:** 4

## 107. [Astrometric modeling of unresolved variable binary systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14690) <a id="link107"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.14690

**Authors:** K. Sivkova, P. Kervella, A. Gallenne, L. Decin, N. Nardetto, F. Arenou, A. Mérand, N. R. Evans, B. Apostolova, M. C. Bailleul, R. S. Rathour, W. Kiviaho, G. Bras, V. Hocdé, L. Breuval, C. Vert, D. P. González

**Abstract:** Gaia DR4 will, for the first time, provide epoch astrometry. When analysing these data, binary sources must be treated carefully, as modelling their astrometry as single stars can bias parallax and proper motion estimates. We developed the vimbinary tool, a framework to simulate and interpret epoch astrometry of unresolved binary systems and to evaluate the impact of model assumptions on the resulting astrometric parameters. We simulated Gaia DR4-like epoch astrometry for a sample of 17 well-characterised unresolved binary systems, including both non-pulsating binaries and systems containing one photometric variable component - variability-induced movers (VIMs). We show that both binary motion and the VIM effect can significantly impact parallax and proper motion measurements, with the magnitude of the effect strongly dependent on the orbital period, photocentric amplitude, and flux ratio of the specific system. We also show that larger time coverage does not necessarily improve parallax precision, in contrast to proper motion, for which precision generally improves with longer baselines. Instead, parallaxes retrieved with binary-system fitting are more accurate than those obtained within the single-star framework.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 4

H. Wright (Ruhr University Bochum, Faculty of Physics and Astronomy, Astronomical Institute), D. Scott (Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1, Canada)

**Abstract:** The images collected in photometric mode by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) instrument of the Euclid satellite are used to model the point-spread function (PSF) of a selection of sources detected in single and combined frames. We used Q1 and DR1 data to improve the development of the PSF module of the near-infrared processing function (NIR PF) and to refine the models currently provided. We explored a few methods normally used to evaluate the quality of the derived models and discuss possible variations related to the position of the sources in the focal plane and to the wavelength and time of the observations. The procedure of fitting the PSF profile, compared to other methods used for flux estimation, such as aperture photometry, indicates that updated models are better than those provided by Q1 images. The current results are in agreement with several key requirements defined for the mission, but there is still room for further improvements, which we plan to investigate and implement in future releases.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 4

## 109. [Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15454) <a id="link109"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.15454

**Authors:** André A. Costa, Valdir B. Bezerra

**Abstract:** The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 4

## 110. [Origin of the angular momentum of filaments in the local Universe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16208) <a id="link110"></a>

**ArXiv ID:** 2611.16208

**Authors:** V. G. Gurzadyan, N. N. Fimin, V. M. Chechetkin

**Abstract:** Velocity gradients compatible with rotation have been reported across certain nearby cosmic filaments. We show that rotational momentum might be generated in filaments in the local Universe in the presence of a cosmological constant (local dark energy) based on the theorem stating the general function for the equivalence of the gravitational field of a sphere and that of a point mass. We investigated how the cosmological constant modifies the finite-time acquisition and retention of angular momentum in an open filamentary core. Although its isotropic force exerts no direct axial torque, rotational motion can be seeded by tidal interactions with surrounding matter and incoming streams. Early tidal torques establish an imbalance in axial angular momentum, while the subsequent orbit crossing amplifies the resulting rotation, and ultimately, the cosmological constant is able to modify tidal-mode growth and finite-time angular momentum delivery.

**Relevance:** 2
**Novelty:** 4

**Abstract:** The Euclid near-infrared processing function (NIR PF) converts the raw observations acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) into calibrated images and source-level products. Following the first implementation delivered with the Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1), the NIR PF has been revised for the first major Euclid Data Release (DR1), with improvements to detector-level processing, calibration, image reconstruction, and quality control. The DR1 processing includes observations covering more than $1900\,\rm{deg}^2$ and has produced $71\,659$ calibrated near-infrared (NIR) images. We assess the performance of the processing chain through extensive astrometric and photometric validation. The astrometric solution reaches an average root-mean-square (RMS) of 10 mas, remaining below 20 mas for 99% of the dithers in all three NISP bands. Temporal variations in the instrumental throughput are typically corrected to a level of 2 mmag RMS, while the relative photometric accuracy reaches 0.9% for sources brighter than 19 mag in $Y_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}$, and $H_\mathrm{E}$, and the residual spatial variations of the photometric calibration across the focal plane are at the level of approximately 10 mmag for the entire sample. Despite some remaining limitations, the DR1 NIR imaging products are consistent with the required astrometric and photometric performance over the large area covered by this release.

**Novelty:** 4
